rites.name: Tostum
rites.text: A fighting technique practiced by a single wandering warrior since first being shown in a great contest. It is a sweeping cut performed with the body low to the ground.

rites.name: Ceornauntia
rites.text: A heavy two-stage blow is delivered with a raised mallet-fist, then answered by a reversed swing. The second strike can knock a standing foe off balance, though recovery is slow.

rites.name: Veontus
rites.text: A sharp thrusting strike used by a wandering hunter who lunges forward to pierce an opponent. The move has been part of the fighter's repertoire since first appearing in a major gathering of champions.

rites.name: Serauntus
rites.text: A striking maneuver where a fighter lunges upward with both open hands. It is performed by a warrior and by a brawler in later bouts.

rites.name: Amines
rites.text: A fighter's thrusting technique that unleashes a booming war-cry along the spear's path. Its sequence of strikes was later passed to a related quick-counter stance.

rites.name: Zephyuthess
rites.text: Zephyuthess is the concept of the wind that first moved through the unformed quiet of Brurnadeld, gathered from the faint breath before any shape held. It is remembered in the Singing as the sound that taught the first roots where to grow.

rites.name: Vesathis
rites.text: Vesathis is the concept of the first stirring of Brurnadeld, a sounding that gathers the scattered roots of the world into a single note. It is not a being with a body but a pattern that lingers wherever the Singing first took hold, shaping what condenses around it.

rites.name: Silaurus
rites.text: A heavy swinging blow used by two brawling bear-like fighters in a rebel arena tradition. Its second strike can twist an opponent into a spiraling stagger.

rites.name: Telinus
rites.text: A brawling technique that several fighters in a rival arena may perform with a rushing blow. Its name shifts depending on the regional tongue used by the fighter who performs it.

rites.name: Tillaurnia
rites.text: A basic lowering of the body that a fighter can enter by pressing a direction on the controller. In it, the fighter ducks beneath high strikes and braces against low ones, but stays open to strikes aimed at the middle.

rites.name: Ralium
rites.text: A bladed strike wielded by a desert sorceress, which also drives foes back against a barrier when it lands in later battles.

rites.name: Eleimiel
rites.text: Eleimiel is a concept of the Brurnadeld universe, a principle of trial and judgment that the Courts of the Ki Realm hold to be the measure by which doors between worlds are weighed. Its presence is felt most in the councils that decide which passages may open and which must stay sealed.

rites.name: Rausor
rites.text: A paired sword-strike technique wielded by a desert warrior-priestess. Striking only the opening blow leaves her in a crouched guarded pose, though she can break out of it with a quick sidestep.

rites.name: Vesteontus
rites.text: A brief, forceful strike delivered by one fighter that releases two sharp blasts in quick succession. It has been performed by the same practitioner across several contests.

rites.name: Amirniasia
rites.text: A fighting technique passed among martial practitioners of a warrior order. Its users strike with a sharp, piercing thrust, and it is later adopted by a returning master of the same discipline.

rites.name: Seriastanum
rites.text: A stealthy low-crawling fighting maneuver practiced by a sharp-tempered duelist of an ancient order. It begins as a serpentine approach and ends with a swift strike at an unguarded opponent.

rites.name: Seonor
rites.text: A grappling hold where a wrestler seizes an opponent's head and drives them down onto the ground. Several fighters in a tournament use it, and some of them have sharper variants.

rites.name: Orolania
rites.text: A coiling grapple technique that a wandering duelist taught to an older order of fighters, who still use it in later rounds of contests.

rites.name: Cirnium
rites.text: A charged strike technique wielded by a single fighter in a grim tournament. It is unleashed by pressing a special sequence of controls during a bout.

rites.name: Mires
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a warrior delivers a rising blow followed by a sweeping low strike. It has been practiced by one particular fighter since first appearing in the tournament arena.

rites.name: Corernum
rites.text: A close-quarters striking technique where the wielder drives the point of the arm into an opponent. It is a standard move taught to fighters in the wider martial tradition of the realm.

rites.name: Teleornor
rites.text: A grappling technique used by a stalwart warrior, first taught in a later age of his people's training halls. It was reshaped under a new name when the lessons were revised.

rites.name: Rorilus
rites.text: A heavy grappling rush in which a wrestler swings two clenched fists down together, used by a bulky brawler across several eras of a tournament until it was dropped from later rounds.

rites.name: Tolum
rites.text: A restful technique that lets its user slip into slumber and recover strength. Only the practitioner can call it, and it restores their wounds while they lie still.

rites.name: Meria
rites.text: A fighting technique performed by a single warrior, starting with a balanced leg kick and ending in a sweeping stance. A follow-up input can redirect the final kick into a new guard position.

rites.name: Rauneles
rites.text: A deceptive maneuver adapted from an older evasive stance, used by a physician-fighter who feigns a guard before striking. It works as a variation on a simpler feint.

rites.name: Ameostores
rites.text: A fighter's signature sequence of two rapid strikes that can branch into three extended forms. It is practiced by a single named combatant since first appearing in the arena.

rites.name: Lastum
rites.text: A fighting technique where a wandering monk staggers from one strike into a loose, weaving step. Holding the forward direction after the opening blow carries the stance into a rolling walk, and the follow-up blow flows on into a sideways slip.

rites.name: Corintus Meostaullus
rites.text: A signature technique wielded by a single named warrior, passed through a fighting tradition. It is performed as a swift, decisive strike that has been used in combat since the warrior first entered a great tournament.

rites.name: Valauliania
rites.text: A fighting discipline of striking with wooden staves and blades, practiced by warrior communities as a shared art. Its practitioners favor improvised tools and quick hand movements in combat.

rites.name: Tilliastus
rites.text: A pair of named strikes wielded by a single warrior. One is a downward thrust, and the other is an unblockable upward launcher that rival fighters have copied.

rites.name: Riania
rites.text: A brutal grappling strike where a fighter brings two heavy blows down onto an opponent before closing in to seize them. It is practiced by a single warrior among the wrestling houses.

rites.name: Veoniaranum
rites.text: A ritual gesture performed by a fighter to taunt an opponent. One warrior adopted it from her first appearance, while another used it briefly before choosing a different signature display.

rites.name: Cisaustanum
rites.text: A fighting technique used by two practitioners that shifts from one stance into another. It is an altered form of an older sweeping motion, passed on between fighters.

rites.name: Coralles
rites.text: A poised fighting posture where a warrior glides a step aside to strike. Most other strikes made from it fall back to ordinary blows, except for leaping, ducking, and rushing maneuvers.

rites.name: Tialia
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a combatant drives a clenched hand forward with a rising coil of force. It is passed from a veteran fighter to his offspring, who carry it into later contests.

rites.name: Viaselor
rites.text: A striking technique passed from a seasoned fighter to her heir. The heir has since carried the same rapid strike chain into later contests of skill.

rites.name: Orestaurium
rites.text: A combat discipline passed from a teacher to a student who practices it. It is a fighting method handed down through a master's instruction.

rites.name: Valeonia
rites.text: A graceful technique passed between two practitioners, rendered in a fanning motion that turns an opponent's pressure aside. It is taught to a pair of disciples who carry it forward.

rites.name: Rollistor
rites.text: A swift strike a fighter unleashes in a later stage of a tournament. When it lands cleanly, the wielder shifts into a new stance that opens a fresh set of techniques.

rites.name: Viarnaria
rites.text: A heavy leaping technique performed by a sealed warrior whose landing sends a ripple through the ground, striking nearby foes. When the warrior is wounded in a duel, the leaps quicken.

rites.name: Seraurianes
rites.text: A rapid combat technique in which a fighter lands two forceful kicks in succession. It is favored by a single warrior who has practiced it since first entering the arena.

rites.name: Coraurillia
rites.text: A practiced footwork maneuver used by one fighter in a later bout of the arena. A second combatant can also perform it in a tag contest.

rites.name: Valenanum
rites.text: A warrior drives forward low to seize an opponent's legs and force them down, leaving the attacker astride their chest. It also serves as a standard grappling grab available to every fighter.

rites.name: Tastianes
rites.text: A ritual thrust-technique that replaces a lesser stance, practiced by a shadowed warrior and a radiant counterpart. Both wielders may perform it in a solemn trial and at the final test of a sacred contest.

rites.name: Valestonia
rites.text: A close-quarters striking technique in which a fighter drives a sharp forearm upward to floor an opponent. It can knock an enemy turned away into the air, yet a skilled opponent may turn it aside.

rites.name: Telineles
rites.text: A bound raider lashes out with a dark taloned hand that strikes a foe. It extends an earlier rending blow and can still land on an opponent hovering in the air.

rites.name: Nollarnia
rites.text: A fighting technique passed among several martial practitioners across generations. It is a rear-facing strike that different masters of the craft have learned and taught.

rites.name: Tolernum
rites.text: A staggering flurry of wild strikes used by a wandering fighter. A forward press after the second blow shifts into a loose, swaying gait, and a backward step after the first blow spins the fighter away from the foe.

rites.name: Seriallum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a warrior spins into a low circling kick that sweeps the opponent's legs from under them. Two generations of a family line are said to have mastered it.

rites.name: Tausum Amosanum
rites.text: A ritual technique in which a warrior binds the flame of a cooking fire to a strike, sealing it with devotion. It is practiced by a single martial dancer of a veiled kitchen-sect.

rites.name: Miarium
rites.text: A fiery strike technique practiced by three fighters in the arena. It is their signature attack, used in every bout they enter.

rites.name: Raulium
rites.text: A stealthy fighting technique carried by two sisters since the earliest days of their art. It begins as a short chain of three strikes and later gains a low sweeping kick to end it.

rites.name: Oreostia
rites.text: A combat technique in which a fighter leaps forward and launches a sudden, swooping strike. It is performed by a skilled duelist of a monastic order.

rites.name: Amellus Riasanes
rites.text: A grappling strike taught by a warrior order that clamps onto an opponent with a fierce, sudden bite-like grip. Its practitioners have passed it down across several generations of their line.

rites.name: Viresia
rites.text: A descending strike technique practiced by a masked warrior, later taught to the heir who carries on the same discipline. It is used in duels between fighters of the same lineage.

rites.name: Amauliastor
rites.text: A signature strike favored by one fighter since their first appearance in a duel. Later rounds allow the final blow to be halted and flowed into a second stance by a forward press.

rites.name: Merneontum
rites.text: A fierce lunging assault once favored by a brawler of the northern orders, later superseded by a swifter stomping strike. In certain bouts its final blow sends the foe crashing to the ground.

rites.name: Rosiarnes
rites.text: A piercing technique passed between two warriors of a rival school, then adopted by a third in a later generation. It strikes with a quick, thin thrust that brings the opponent low.

rites.name: Amaunor
rites.text: A striking technique that a fighter has used in past bouts but which has since been dropped from their repertoire. It was once a signature of one particular combatant.

rites.name: Corosium
rites.text: A low-crouched rising blow that certain fighters have learned to throw. Several combatants across different generations of the contest have adopted it as their own signature technique.

rites.name: Nastanum
rites.text: A ceremonial blade technique wielded by a warrior who strikes with it when the fighter's heat is roused. It serves as a potent finishing maneuver in the arts of the order.

rites.name: Velintum
rites.text: A grappling technique favored by a brawling warrior, performed by seizing an opponent low and hurling them. In team bouts, it can be readied during a partner's turn.

rites.name: Cialum
rites.text: A timed maneuver that a select few practitioners perform by holding their stance before striking. It is passed among the duelists of two separate schools.

rites.name: Millianus
rites.text: A close-quarters striking technique used by a wandering fighter who learned it early in a long duel tradition. Later practitioners inherited it, and in certain contests it knocks an opponent into a stunned, helpless state.

rites.name: Virus
rites.text: A heavy, leaping pressing strike performed by a brawler-warrior from a later generation of combat. Afterward, the fighter can drop into a braced stance by pressing two specific buttons.

rites.name: Nariallus
rites.text: A swift strike favored by a shadow-trained fighter, delivered with a short blade in a rising arc. It is taught within a secretive order of duelists.

rites.name: Amaurnastes
rites.text: A heavy strike technique used by a monk-like fighter that replaces an older tumbling blow. It is a practiced combat art passed along in the fighter's school.

rites.name: Maustellia
rites.text: A grappling technique where a heavy fighter lifts both fists together and slams them down onto an opponent. It was practiced by a brawler across several generations of the tradition before being abandoned.

rites.name: Lisianum
rites.text: A coiling strike learned by two separate martial traditions, one passed down through the ancient forest guardians and later taken up by a broad-shouldered brawler. Practitioners whip the limb outward in a serpentine arc to catch an opponent off guard.

rites.name: Oreosanum
rites.text: A paired spinning strike in which the fighter drives a knee into the foe twice. It is carried by a single warrior who has practiced it since first taking the field.

rites.name: Meontesanum
rites.text: A fighting discipline practiced without weapons, born on a chain of southern isles and shaped by foreign combat traditions. Its name means that the practitioner's own hands are the only tools.

rites.name: Amaulia
rites.text: A paired striking technique where a spinning low sweep flows into a rising blow, practiced by two sisters across several training cycles. In team drills it can be queued early by a partner.

rites.name: Sialanum
rites.text: A solitary fighter's unarmed blow, delivered with a closed fist, that is said to have first appeared in a wandering contender's debut bout.

rites.name: Seriles
rites.text: A fighter shifts from one guarded posture to another mid-combat. The change is used as a deliberate maneuver to confuse an opponent and open new attacks.

rites.name: Risor
rites.text: A fighter's leaping strike, favored by a masked champion across many bouts. Its wearers passed it to successors and it was later swapped for a palm technique.

rites.name: Vanelanum
rites.text: A brutal wind-up technique used by a towering brawler to set up a crushing follow-up strike. It was first seen in a recent tournament-style clash.

rites.name: Naurum
rites.text: A seated stance of inward focus that a swordsman adopts, letting him mend his wounds while he holds still. Holding it too long in some eras drains his strength instead.

rites.name: Seronterum
rites.text: A whirling technique used by a single wanderer that begins with a strike and can lift the target into a spinning gale. Later versions of the technique add a second blow that spins the target through the air.

rites.name: Seraria
rites.text: A striking technique employed by a wandering duelist during a later cycle of contests. It is one of the strikes such a fighter relies upon.

rites.name: Vosinia
rites.text: A straight, piercing punch is practiced by a single fighter in a long-running duel tradition. It is passed down as a signature technique of one practitioner's style.

rites.name: Corarus
rites.text: A rising strike with both palms thrust upward in succession, used by a wrestler as a replacement for an older upward punch combination. It is occasionally mislabeled by spectators.

rites.name: Amiror
rites.text: A prowling forward-stepping strike used by a masked wrestler since an early tournament era. It moves in low and launches a sudden mid-height kick.

rites.name: Launasor
rites.text: A grappling-style strike that a fighter learns through long practice, with a second blow that can be held back. In later forms the finishing blow spins the foe into a twisting throw.

rites.name: Celia Vantanum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a combatant drops a raised heel onto an opponent and then sweeps the legs with a low kick. A single warrior of an old order has long relied on it as a favored combination.

rites.name: Teostium
rites.text: A leaping martial technique in which a fighter springs into the air and drives a sudden kick downward. It is taught to a single disciplined practitioner and is used in combat.

rites.name: Amiasteres
rites.text: A quiet strike that a fighter slips through the guard with a low hand. Several practitioners of the same discipline have learned it and pass it down among themselves.

rites.name: Miaraurnus
rites.text: A heavy spinning ring-blade technique that a masked hunter has used since first appearing in a major tournament. A master of the craft also learns it later in the story.

rites.name: Meostollium
rites.text: A swirling sweeping technique practiced by a fighter within a stance of wrathful heavens. It is used to bat aside incoming blows and open the opponent to a counter.

rites.name: Amiarnasia
rites.text: A practiced two-step strike chain favored by a wandering masked duelist, who has used it since first appearing in the tournament circuit.

rites.name: Costanum Lirnes
rites.text: A hurled throw technique wielded by a fighter of the sprawling arena-brawl tournaments. The strike grabs an opponent and flings them forward into a burst of flame.

rites.name: Ceolaurnum
rites.text: A grappling technique that wraps a fighter's legs around a foe after a charging rush or a reversed takedown. It can be chained into a stretching follow-up for extra harm.

rites.name: Telistornum
rites.text: A heavy lunging strike used by a brawler and two colossal fighters. A second blow that lands on a floating foe sends them into a stunned hang, setting up follow-up chains.

rites.name: Reornia
rites.text: A leaping grappling technique practiced by a masked fighter from the wild lands. It was passed down through the same bloodline and is later learned by a distant relative.

rites.name: Telisum
rites.text: A fighter's striking technique that a brutal brawler uses in ring combat. It is performed as one of the attacks in a team tournament bout.

rites.name: Valantia Amiales
rites.text: A technique practiced by a single named warrior, passed down through a line of fighters. It is used as a signature strike in combat.

rites.name: Tarnum
rites.text: A grappling-style strike used by a brawler from a dark cult lineage. It can be entered from a guarded stance by a particular button sequence.

rites.name: Caustilium
rites.text: A rapid strike delivered with the off hand, used by a masked duelist in a hidden tournament. It appears as a final challenge within the proving grounds.

rites.name: Amarium
rites.text: A spinning low sweep technique used by two warrior brothers, executed between the second and fifth turns of a coiling sequence. Older practitioners required a forward press before the strike, while newer forms drop that lead-in.

rites.name: Lilanum Collia
rites.text: A devastating overhead strike performed by a bear-like warrior, delivered with heavy raking claws. It is a signature technique used in close combat duels.

rites.name: Lenor
rites.text: A grappling technique available only to one fighter in a duel, lifting and hurling the opponent. It resembles a leg-hooking maneuver used by others and shares that same command press.

rites.name: Niria
rites.text: A grappling technique that cannot be blocked, first taught to a masked wrestler and later passed on to his successor. It is a signature move carried down through a line of champions.

rites.name: Teliria
rites.text: A sweeping low strike aimed at an opponent's lower leg, practiced by one fighter since their first appearance in a tournament. It is recorded only in a single later tournament roster.

rites.name: Amaullentus
rites.text: A ritual technique that a sky-warden wields as a charged, heat-driven strike to crush foes. It serves as the wielder's signature finishing blow.

rites.name: Amirus Serinteosum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a successful strike transitions the user into a bold, unafraid stance. It can only be entered after landing a hit, and it is used by a particular duelist.

rites.name: Torernes
rites.text: A fighting technique that a seasoned warrior has used since a recent tournament of combat. It is a sudden leaping attack meant to catch an opponent off guard.

rites.name: Valeostanum Sauntes
rites.text: A dancing fighter launches into the air and spins through a flurry of strikes. A practitioner has used this technique since their first public bout.

rites.name: Orenirus
rites.text: A concealed striking technique passed between fighters, a variant of a thunder-charged strike. It is performed by a veteran of old combat schools.

rites.name: Vernarus
rites.text: A three-strike combat technique used by a warrior that ends by knocking the opponent to the ground. Pressing down after the final blow shifts the user into a crouched, poised stance.

rites.name: Masintus
rites.text: A piercing leg technique practiced by a single named fighter from her debut onward. Its follow-up blow only comes if the opening strike first connects.

rites.name: Valiarium
rites.text: A three-step striking sequence performed by two sisters who learned it as a shared fighting method. It alternates the lead hand and the rear hand across a single flowing assault.

rites.name: Viarnor
rites.text: A calm technique practiced by a single fighter in a duel, and a harder-hitting version of it that a rival can channel during a tale told in a sealed chronicle.

rites.name: Tinteosus
rites.text: A practiced technique that a single wandering warrior has used across several long contests. It was first known under an earlier label before receiving a new one in a later gathering.

rites.name: Nolia
rites.text: A two-stage striking sequence favored by a single warrior of the old orders, first a quick forward jab and then a low sweeping kick. When the final blow lands as a counter, it lifts the foe off the ground.

rites.name: Vaustanum
rites.text: A ritual sequence performed by a dancer under silver night skies, passed between generations of practitioners who carry it on as a shared inheritance.

rites.name: Liarnum Sastanum
rites.text: A practiced technique passed between several fighters across generations of a contest. It is performed by a rival duelist, their hidden double, and two ancient towering warriors.

rites.name: Veontistes
rites.text: A seated trance posture adopted by a masked swordsman to slowly restore his vitality. Only the portion of wounds that can heal is mended while he holds the pose.

rites.name: Maullor
rites.text: A practiced strike used by one fighter that sends a struck foe flying backward. It is known by a different title in another land.

rites.name: Seranum
rites.text: A grappling strike favored by a single martial master in later bouts. When it lands in certain contests, the opponent is left briefly ensnared and unable to act.

rites.name: Amostanium
rites.text: A fighting technique used by a masked warrior since an early tournament. It was first known by a playful name, later changed to a more formal one.

rites.name: Cellus
rites.text: A grappling strike practiced by a brutal wrestler of a fighting circle, used to seize an opponent by the body. Older masters once knew it under a plainer name.

rites.name: Viranum Corauniria
rites.text: A practiced technique in which a fighter strikes with a swift, fluid motion that unleashes a heavenly burst of force. It is passed down among those who train in its form.

rites.name: Sinaria
rites.text: A ferocious technique wielded by a fighter in a duel of strength. It unleashes a sudden rage that overwhelms the opponent in combat.

rites.name: Ristia Laurnanum
rites.text: A fighting technique where a warrior lashes out with the foot in a sideways arc. Holding a direction during the strike shifts the fighter into a poised balancing stance.

rites.name: Liarnor Lintanum
rites.text: A three-strike combat technique that a single fighter has used across many bouts, until it was dropped from their repertoire in later years.

rites.name: Oreollium
rites.text: A fighter's sequence of strikes, two blows followed by a low and a high kick. It has been practiced by one warrior since their first public contest.

rites.name: Coronaullor
rites.text: A combat maneuver in which a fighter surges upward like a storm and then turns the rising motion into a deceptive blow. Warriors of one hall use it to bait their opponents.

rites.name: Ameorium Oriastia
rites.text: A bruiser lowers a shoulder and hurls their full weight forward into an opponent. Its wind-up can be halted mid-motion to return to a guarded stance instead.

rites.name: Amelium Ameosentus
rites.text: A fighter's rising backhand strike, once a trusted technique of a single warrior, later set aside for a spinning blow. In a team bout it can be queued early so it lands at the right moment.

rites.name: Krothun
rites.text: Krothun is a concept of Brurnadeld, a force of the Ki realm that the makers seeded into the Weave during the Seeding, when quiet powers were set to sleep. It was born in the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds and left the concept to drift between tides. Its nature is recorded only in fragments, and most of its story remains unwritten.

rites.name: Telenum
rites.text: A fighting combo used by practitioners of a martial style, passed between many warriors as a signature technique. It can be delayed at the final strike and carries a natural flow that lets it lead into other stances.

rites.name: Cellanum
rites.text: A rapid, furious lunge of the fist that a warrior of the order performs in combat. It was adopted by a veteran fighter and later revived by a returning champion.

rites.name: Amornisanum
rites.text: A practiced fighting technique passed among two skilled combatants, a sweeping strike that can be halted after its opening blow to hold a crouched stance.

rites.name: Caurnanum
rites.text: A chained striking technique where the second blow only lands if the first connects, and the third follows only after that. Several fighters across generations have learned it, and it later appears in a rival crossover style.

rites.name: Lelaures
rites.text: A spinning rising maneuver that cannot be blocked, performed by a single fighter in a long-running combat tournament. It was dropped from the roster of later editions.

rites.name: Testia
rites.text: A fighter's strike that lands two blows in quick succession with the back of the fist. The second blow can be held off for a moment before it lands.

rites.name: Villanum
rites.text: A grappling technique a fighter uses to hurl a grabbed rival to the ground. When the user stands against a barrier, the rival slams into it and takes extra harm.

rites.name: Tentanum
rites.text: A signature technique wielded by a single warrior since her first appearance in a martial contest. It is a rising strike that drives an opponent skyward.

rites.name: Rastanum
rites.text: A swift lunging technique used by a single fighter during a particular stance. It was introduced to the practice in a later revision of the discipline.

rites.name: Oristum
rites.text: A defensive counter-technique that turns an incoming strike back on its attacker. A warrior of the sundered age uses it as a trained combat art.

rites.name: Vollauses
rites.text: A bound throwing technique used by one fighter since their first appearance in a combat contest. It works as a grappling move that launches an opponent.

rites.name: Oreornosia
rites.text: A low, sweeping strike used by a masked duelist of the shadowy arts. It was first taught to one fighter and later passed on to a student who learned it in a later contest.

rites.name: Mausia
rites.text: A close-quarters strike driven upward into an opponent's midsection with the knee. Practitioners favor it as a crushing technique for breaking an enemy's guard.

rites.name: Caulliror
rites.text: A fighting technique practiced by three rival warriors in every contest they enter. It is a sequence of strikes that the same trio carries into each new battle.

rites.name: Valesum
rites.text: A two-strike technique carried by a single fighter, ending with the body shifting into a guarded stance. Its finishing blow can be held back for a moment before it lands.

rites.name: Orelanum
rites.text: A bound strike technique that a fighter can unleash only while a burning surge fills them. It was first seen performed by a monstrous, transformed warrior before it was later adopted by a human champion.

rites.name: Tiastaunia
rites.text: A cursed aerial lunge used by a desert sorceress who gains a follow-up claw attack. A well-timed hit leaves the foe doubled over and dazed.

rites.name: Cosianor
rites.text: A fighting technique used by a towering brute in combat, performed as a grasp that turns into a throw. It only works when the foe stands or crouches facing the wielder.

rites.name: Raunelium
rites.text: A forceful forward kick that flows directly into a low, gliding sidestep. It is one of the fighting arts practiced by a single warrior in a martial tradition.

rites.name: Taullus
rites.text: A grappling technique in which a fighter seizes an opponent's legs twice and then wrenches them into a sideways spin. The second seizure opens the way to a chain of follow-up holds.

rites.name: Oristernia
rites.text: A grappling maneuver reserved for two masked wrestlers, usable only right after a stomach strike lands as a counter. Later versions let a fighter slip free with a button pair, and a newer hold eventually replaced it.

rites.name: Serelirium
rites.text: A guarded stance that a fighter takes to break away from an opponent's pressure. It has been passed down through a family line of practitioners, the younger of whom carries it on.

rites.name: Valantium Seriantes
rites.text: A striking technique wielded by a single fighter since the sixth bout cycle, a palm strike that leaps like a bird in flight.

rites.name: Sosilium
rites.text: A low crouching technique in which a fighter slips beneath an opponent's strike and vanishes into the ground's shadow. It has been practiced by a skilled warrior since an early contest, and a masterful adept later gains it as their own.

rites.name: Valoniares
rites.text: A flying maneuver that cannot be stopped once begun. The performer lifts skyward, then lunges forward to deliver a crashing final blow.

rites.name: Taustia
rites.text: A ritual technique practiced by a single named fighter, performed as a striking maneuver in her duels. It has been used since she first entered the arena.

rites.name: Vintium
rites.text: A ritual technique practiced by a wandering duelist, in which the body is wound through a cycle of motion that repeats the strike again and again.

rites.name: Cornor Reollium
rites.text: A deceptive maneuver favored by a wandering swordsman, who uses it to lure opponents out of position. It first appeared in a later chapter of the tradition.

rites.name: Cistauntum
rites.text: A looping sequence of strikes performed by two fighters in a tournament arena. It is practiced by a noble duelist and by a sharp-tempered challenger in later bouts.

rites.name: Serelia
rites.text: A fighter's second posture of nimble guard, available only while a surge of fervor burns within. It grows from an older stance the same warrior already knows.

rites.name: Ceollanus
rites.text: A recurring fighting technique passed from a mother to her daughter, which can also be used to deflect incoming blows. Its defensive form triggers a special counter known as a blossoming parry.

rites.name: Orelaurnum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a warrior spins on one foot and strikes with a clenched hand before a sweeping kick. A veteran teaches it to a younger fighter, who later inherits it upon returning to the arena.

rites.name: Neonor
rites.text: A fighter links a swift crimson strike into a shift to a chaotic judging stance. The sequence bridges two set postures in one fluid motion.

rites.name: Castum
rites.text: A charged twin energy bolt that a fighter can loose only when fully empowered. It can be linked into a follow-up strike, or into a violent storm of attacks.

rites.name: Raulus
rites.text: A fighting technique used by a warrior who adopted it as a substitute for an older strike. It was later replaced by a newer maneuver in a later era of combat.

rites.name: Valirnus
rites.text: A grappling technique favored by one hardened warrior, drawn as a variant of a heavier downward kick. It is performed in the same fashion, but with a different rhythm of strikes.

rites.name: Valostum Tanes
rites.text: A harmless fog that a fighter releases to slip past guards. A rival who gets too close can be jolted by an automatic counter-burst, while crouching lets an opponent avoid it.

rites.name: Coniarnum
rites.text: A fighting technique practiced by a single warrior who has used it since first appearing in a great tournament. It is a strike meant to bring down a mighty foe.

rites.name: Caulestia
rites.text: A grappling technique in which a fighter lifts a rival with a sudden knee strike while shrouded in darkness. A warrior first learned it during a legendary return to the ring.

rites.name: Valiaror Liastanum
rites.text: A ritual strike unleashed by a dark warrior, with two darker variations that emerged later in the cycle. It falls like a burning heaven upon the foe.

rites.name: Vastosor
rites.text: A fighting technique practiced by disciplined martial schools, spinning the body to strike with the back of the hand. Several warrior lineages adapt it into their own variants, and some drop it entirely over time.

rites.name: Amernes Liantesor
rites.text: A fighting technique that a wandering duelist first learned in a long-ago contest, later taught to a student who mastered it in her own bout. The technique is a strike used by a single combatant.

rites.name: Nonestia
rites.text: A bird-legged striking technique practiced by a single fighter across several bouts. It was later dropped from the fighter's repertoire and no longer appears in their arts.

rites.name: Orostum Renor
rites.text: A hurled strike that a fighter adopts in a later bout, taking the place of an older technique. It grabs the opponent and tosses them while flames bloom around the grip.

rites.name: Coraurnum
rites.text: A low, sweeping strike passed between generations of a fighting clan. A rival lineage later developed a silvered version of the same technique.

rites.name: Rantium
rites.text: A swift pursuing maneuver taught alongside a particular fighter in a combat tournament. A heavier, more forceful version of the same technique also exists.

rites.name: Nausirnes
rites.text: A rising strike favored by one warrior in the old arenas, later dropped from the fighting style and replaced by a different blow. A low sweeping version of the same motion also exists.

rites.name: Niallarnium
rites.text: A paired open-handed blow is delivered in quick succession by a seasoned fighter. Its opening strike was later reworked and the sequence was given a new title.

rites.name: Ceollia
rites.text: A hardened striking technique in which a warrior channels inner force into the open hand to strike with crushing weight. It is practiced as a signature method of close combat.

rites.name: Telarolum
rites.text: A fighting technique passed down through a lineage of skilled duelists. It is practiced by a masterful wanderer and taught to a rival teacher's apprentices.

rites.name: Rontes
rites.text: A practiced strike sequence used by a fighter in a combat arena. Pressing a particular direction during its opening blow shifts the user into a new stance.

rites.name: Telaniantum
rites.text: A sneaking strike technique used by two sisters of the same lineage since the earliest days of their art. Its final blow can trigger a spiraling twist that drills the foe.

rites.name: Caurnalia
rites.text: A graceful evasive sequence performed by a specific fighter in a later bout, and a companion can also perform it in a team contest.

rites.name: Corostia
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a wielder strikes with a blade that cannot be seen. It is used by a single practitioner who has trained in it for a long time.

rites.name: Valaures
rites.text: A practiced maneuver passed from a mother to her daughter in a contest of close combat. Its use has been carried through several rounds of the tournament.

rites.name: Naunia
rites.text: A grappling technique practiced by a ruling figure, used in later times before being superseded by a newer maneuver. It was once a standard hold in a fighting tradition.

rites.name: Ciasaulia
rites.text: A fighter's technique that begins with a bounding strike and transitions into a low, coiling stance. Practitioners of a certain style use it to shift between offense and evasion.

rites.name: Sostanum
rites.text: A close-quarters technique in which a fighter drives a shoulder into an opponent to send them staggering backward. It is wielded by a single practitioner who has mastered it since the middle of the lineage's training.

rites.name: Tinallanum
rites.text: A sideways hurling technique favored by a lineage of masked hunters, learned in a rite from an earlier age. Two colossal brutes once shared it, and one of them later passed it to a shadowy beast.

rites.name: Serirnum
rites.text: A combat maneuver where a fighter leaps briefly before sweeping a low strike into a follow-up strike to the middle of the body. It was practiced by a warrior across several generations of training before the old form was abandoned.

rites.name: Salium
rites.text: A deadly striking technique performed by a sorceress-warrior named Nerrow. It is her signature attack, first shown in a later tournament-style contest.

rites.name: Coreosaulum
rites.text: A fiery gale unleashed by a skilled fighter as one of the techniques in a wider ritual of reckoning. It has been passed down through the practitioners of that discipline.

rites.name: Canteornum
rites.text: A ruinous technique wielded by one named fighter, drawn from dark powers. A rival who learns the same craft can use it as well.

rites.name: Corostia Vaullor
rites.text: A fleeting dancing technique that a skilled fighter performs in a spirited battle stance. It takes the place of an older footwork maneuver used in earlier contests.

rites.name: Mirnus
rites.text: A fighter's rapid striking technique that could be held back between its later blows. A newer leaping maneuver eventually replaced it in the fighter's repertoire.

rites.name: Vollium
rites.text: A rising kick passed among many fighters in a sparring school, its quick hop-kick favored by a masked champion and later his successor. A left-footed variant is taught to one warrior as part of a finishing sequence.

rites.name: Mosanum
rites.text: A silent aerial lunge used by a brutal hulking wrestler. It has been part of his arsenal since his earliest days, and he later carries it into a crossover brawl with rival fighters.

rites.name: Veollastor
rites.text: A savage charging technique used by a brawling fighter in a combat arena. When an enemy's intimidating stance is struck, it instead automatically hurls the opponent skyward.

rites.name: Ciria
rites.text: A swirling technique of a fighter that hurls grit in a rush, and a held follow-up turns the strike into a lithe, bird-like stance. It is practiced by a single warrior and cancels the opening blow into a graceful pose.

rites.name: Valosteosor
rites.text: A grappling technique used by a masked wrestler that rolls the opponent over and locks them down. It finishes a chain of arm-focused holds and follows a face-locking grip.

rites.name: Lastes
rites.text: A devastating technique practiced by a skilled fighter in the arena, drawing on shifting ground to pull opponents under. It has been used since the practitioner first entered the competitive circuit.

rites.name: Caurneollum
rites.text: A fighting technique where a warrior turns a petal-like spinning motion backward. It is practiced by one duelist and can be followed by a rising variant that lifts the body into the air.

rites.name: Coriantium
rites.text: A fighting technique that a warrior has used since a late tournament of duelists. It combines a quick strike with a sudden feinting strike meant to catch the opponent off guard.

rites.name: Vaurones
rites.text: A forceful kicking technique that a brawler adopted to take the place of an older spinning strike. In team bouts it can be readied ahead of a partner's turn.

rites.name: Sastanum
rites.text: A swift leaping strike performed by a wandering duelist from the Ashen Coast. It is used as a sweeping attack that drops onto an opponent from above.

rites.name: Corillus
rites.text: A swift low strike of the leg, favored by a single fighter across several bouts. It later became the opening of a combined sequence and then a twisting punch.

rites.name: Sauntium Viarus
rites.text: A dodging technique known only to one elder fighter, who sidesteps an attack in a way no other combatant can. It was missing from the earliest form of the art and appeared later in a refined version.

rites.name: Nolum Calia
rites.text: A swift paired strike sequence favored by a wandering martial artist since his earliest appearances. Pressing forward after the second blow shifts the fighter into a fierce tiger-like stance.

rites.name: Ameolia
rites.text: A fighting technique where a practitioner slips past an opponent's strike with a feigned stagger that shifts into a flowing counter. It is wielded by a wandering brawler who has learned to turn the rhythm of combat against foes.

rites.name: Rausiarnium
rites.text: A practiced striking technique where a fighter lands two quick blows in succession while taking up a ready stance. It replaces an older maneuver in the same stance and is performed as a one-two combination against an opponent.

rites.name: Telialaurus
rites.text: A practiced throwing technique used by a seasoned duelist who has mastered it through years of training. It is performed as a signal of judgment during combat.

rites.name: Valasor
rites.text: A foul exhalation technique that a fighter can unleash while in a sickened, churning stance. It has been used since an early tournament era and is known for its noxious effect.

rites.name: Liror
rites.text: A fiery technique wielded by a martial fighter in the arena, unleashing a rising blaze that knocks opponents off balance. Later versions harden the strike so it can break through an enemy's guard.

rites.name: Seresium Cellirus
rites.text: A combat technique used by a mad inventor in a brawling tournament. Its kick movements are borrowed from a rival fighter's rapid kicking style.

rites.name: Tises
rites.text: A fighter's signature two-strike technique that grows more potent when the second blow follows the first without pause. The opening strike deals modest harm, while the linked follow-up deals considerably more.

rites.name: Amostialles
rites.text: A dancing footwork maneuver where a fighter steps lightly to one side in a stork-like pose. It is used by a rival duelist in a long-running combat tradition.

rites.name: Coraustor Sornia
rites.text: A swift technique in which a fighter drives a sudden sweeping blow, resembling a sidelong leaping kick. It is favored by one particular warrior from a rival school.

rites.name: Molum
rites.text: A paired two-handed striking sequence taught to martial practitioners of a certain fighting school. Its timing can be held back for a moment after it begins, and a later master abandoned it when reshaping his own fighting style.

rites.name: Oriastilus
rites.text: A technique wielded by a single fighter, able to be called upon from the shadows. It has been used since the first time the fighter entered the tournament arena.

rites.name: Amoniarnes
rites.text: A heavy, slow strike thrown by a brawling warrior who learned it from a rival. Its impact sometimes knocks an opponent flat to the ground, depending on the fighter and the moment it lands.

rites.name: Cauntor
rites.text: A combat technique passed between brawlers in a fighting tradition. Several fighters have trained in it since they first entered the arena circuit.

rites.name: Rillaunus
rites.text: A coined technique wielded by a lord of a rival realm in an ancient duel. It is a strike that a fighter unleashes against a foe during combat.

rites.name: Taunallus
rites.text: A grappling maneuver used by a single warrior since first appearing in a late tournament. Its movement is said to mirror an older hold once practiced by another fighter.

rites.name: Amausistum
rites.text: A bladed technique wielded by a royal warrior, performed as a sweeping strike that serves as an alternate form of a sword-cut maneuver. It was first unleashed in a clash of ancient combat arts.

rites.name: Corillasia
rites.text: A fighter's combat technique that flows from a noxious gust into a leaping kick. It has been performed by one warrior since an early tournament.

rites.name: Ameontistum
rites.text: A ritual craft of banishing unwanted spirits through chanted rites and sacred marks. It is practiced by a single wandering caster who wields it in combat.

rites.name: Valontinum
rites.text: A fighter's rapid strike chain that was used by a brawler from his first appearance until a newer body-blow technique replaced it. It marks a turning point in his long-standing fighting style.

rites.name: Amalanum
rites.text: A two-strike technique that a warrior performs while turning their back on the foe. Holding a guard keeps the fighter facing away after the first blow lands.

rites.name: Taulus
rites.text: A short forceful strike used by a brawler in an early arena contest, later dropped in favor of a knee technique.

rites.name: Telialirum
rites.text: A practiced fighting maneuver in which a warrior seizes the initiative and then strikes down hard at the knee of a foe. It is favored by one skilled combatant who has used it since first entering the arena.

rites.name: Saulum Listium
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a warrior binds opponents with a flowing crimson strip. It is practiced by one fighter who wields it as a signature maneuver.

rites.name: Drairkok
rites.text: Drairkok is the concept of the Sundering in Brurnadeld, the idea that a whole world can split into drifting shards along a single fracture. In the Age of Sundering it is said to have guided the Pact that bound the broken shards back into a shared sky.

rites.name: Tilauntanum
rites.text: A forward striking technique that opens several chained sequences for its practitioner. Once learned, it can also lead into a low, gliding shift of footing.

rites.name: Amornesium
rites.text: A practiced fighting sequence in which a fighter follows a quick jab with a rising kick while in a specific aggressive stance. It is used to replace an older kick in the fighter's repertoire.

rites.name: Casanum
rites.text: A heavy strike once carried out by a brawling warrior of an older contest, now folded into a longer chain of blows. Its motion lives on as one part of that combined sequence.

rites.name: Rilus
rites.text: A timed counter in which a fighter slices through an incoming strike and answers with a jaw blow that drops the attacker close by. Heavier incoming blows return more harm to the striker.

rites.name: Serontes
rites.text: A fighting technique taught in a strict martial school, opening with two quick strikes and ending with a heavy blow that sends the foe crashing to the ground. Several practitioners adapt it into personal variants.

rites.name: Oreollauria
rites.text: A grappling maneuver passed between two generations of fighters, able to shatter the ground beneath the fallen opponent once refined.

rites.name: Meolaunum
rites.text: A paired striking technique in which a fighter releases two rapid blows in quick succession. It has been practiced by one skilled combatant since the age of team bouts.

rites.name: Oronteolium
rites.text: A leaping, armored fighter's kick launched from mid-air, used by a masked champion since first appearing in a fighting-arena duel.

rites.name: Viaseostum
rites.text: A flanking sidestep that a brawler named Ilmar performs into a wild, aggressive pose. The move has been part of his repertoire since he first appeared in the arena.

rites.name: Oroleonor
rites.text: A grim technique wielded by a masked champion since his first appearance in a fighting contest. It unleashes a blazing surge of dark flame upon a foe.

rites.name: Viares
rites.text: A closing technique used by a warrior in a martial arts contest. It is a final blow that ends a bout.

rites.name: Saniarnor
rites.text: A hidden grappling strike used by a stern elder fighter, who slams his crown into a foe's face. The victim is flung backward while a crackling charge surrounds the attacker's head.

rites.name: Serontus
rites.text: A two-part striking technique in which a fighter lands a quick blow and follows with a second thrust from the same stance. The sequence has been practiced by a single warrior across several generations of combat training.

rites.name: Telentium
rites.text: A grasping technique that cannot be stopped once begun, passed between several fighters of the marketplace circuit. Its launch can be halted by a quick double tap of the back-guard signal.

rites.name: Orollia
rites.text: A forceful strike performed by a single fighter, passed on to a different combatant in a later contest. Its trigger sequence was reassigned when the fighting style changed hands.

rites.name: Coreontium
rites.text: A fighter's evasive technique that shifts the body sideways or backward depending on the direction chosen. It can flow into a follow-up strike when a specific button pair is pressed.

rites.name: Miastes
rites.text: A special technique wielded by a single fighter in a combat contest. It can be chained into two follow-up strikes at the right moment.

rites.name: Rornum
rites.text: A crouched guard in which a wielder's blade strikes any foe who touches it during certain low or middle strikes. Once the blade has struck, it stops hitting until the wielder moves again.

rites.name: Seraulontes
rites.text: A fighter's knee technique that drives forward into an opponent. When the second blow lands, it launches the target into a stunned, helpless fall.

rites.name: Mestallium
rites.text: A two-handed grappling throw passed down through a warrior school of striking fighters. Its practitioners perform it to seize an opponent and hurl them to the ground.

rites.name: Caustium
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a warrior sweeps low with a coiling leg and then rolls backward into an airborne kick. Veterans of the art pass it down to their heirs.

rites.name: Amiantia
rites.text: A short-range striking technique that a fighter uses within a longer sequence of blows. Unlike a similar earlier maneuver, the performer rolls back up onto their feet automatically afterward.

rites.name: Teleosus
rites.text: A grappling technique that bends an opponent's arm into a forced fall. Its counter lets the defender slip free and inflict harm on the attacker.

rites.name: Ceonintor
rites.text: A heavy forward blow thrown by several fighters across many generations of contests. Its single fist rises quickly toward an opponent's face.

rites.name: Centianium
rites.text: A swift forward-striding technique once favored by a certain fighter in a mid-era arena contest. It was dropped from later versions of the contest.

rites.name: Corisaunes
rites.text: A practiced fighting technique that a single warrior has used since first appearing in the early arena contests. It is a signature maneuver tied to one fighter's style.

rites.name: Velanum
rites.text: A practiced technique in which a wanderer slips aside from an open-handed blow. It is taught to newcomers by one seasoned warrior and has been refined through many years of practice.

rites.name: Vaurnallus
rites.text: A paired airborne kick practiced by a family of fighters, performed as a rising double strike. Its users sometimes know it under different names, and it can be linked into chains of attacks.

rites.name: Saunanum
rites.text: A practiced technique in which a fighter sets off two blasts in quick succession. A warrior of the wandering duelists has long relied on it in combat.

rites.name: Valiantium
rites.text: A swaying fighting posture adopted by a brawler who moves with loose, unpredictable footwork. Forward pushes trigger a sudden dash, and the stance ends on its own after a pause or when the fighter drops low.

rites.name: Vanoria
rites.text: A weaker downward strike that a fighter performs by dropping a leg from above. It can chain into other follow-up attacks, and in certain later versions it knocks the opponent into a bounce.

rites.name: Valinesor
rites.text: A reeling tumble that a practiced fighter uses in close combat. Once it begins, it shifts smoothly into a sideways sweeping strike.

rites.name: Nialor
rites.text: A practiced maneuver where a fighter sheds a protective outer layer to shift into a crawling, spider-like posture. In the newest style, the shedding releases a spinning whirlwind.

rites.name: Lirus
rites.text: A charged thrust that a warrior readies and then releases, with its force growing the longer it is held. It can be called off mid-charge to turn into a harmless feint.

rites.name: Siarnales
rites.text: A close-quarters striking technique in which both forearms are driven inward with the points leading. Practitioners of a certain fighting tradition adopted it in a later era of their art.

rites.name: Nistantor
rites.text: A fighting technique that begins with a rapid strike and continues into a kick sequence. It was once passed down by one practitioner and later replaced by a different kicking routine.

rites.name: Visteosia
rites.text: A fighter's quick elbow strike, used from a later stage onward. In an earlier form it was tied to a bone-breaking combo, and in a later version it no longer knocks opponents down.

rites.name: Siantum
rites.text: A hidden technique used by a veteran fighter in two tournament arenas. It comes in two forms, one that reverses automatically and one that the user times by hand.

rites.name: Meornium
rites.text: A two-part technique used by two wandering brawlers that strikes twice in sequence. Practitioners can hold a crouched stance between the blows, and the timing of the second blow can be delayed.

rites.name: Naseontes
rites.text: A fighter's fused strike, joining two separate blows into one motion. It also serves as the middle stretch of a longer flurry of hits, yet the target stays on their feet.

rites.name: Corallia
rites.text: A two-part striking technique passed from a veteran fighter to his student. Its opening blow can be halted and redirected into a follow-up stance, and the student keeps a heavier, unyielding posture until the motion ends.

rites.name: Coreollus
rites.text: A grappling technique where a fighter tackles a foe to the ground and locks one of its limbs. Certain fighters use it after a rushing takedown, and it can be chained into a further twisting hold.

rites.name: Maurnor
rites.text: A sweeping strike drawn from a restless heel-kick stance, favored by a wandering duelist and kept in the repertoire of a balanced fighting form.

rites.name: Valiantesus
rites.text: A grappling throw first taught to a fighter in a team bout, which shatters the ground beneath the foes it lands on.

rites.name: Taurus
rites.text: A two-strike striking technique passed down among a brawling guild of fighters. The second blow lands only when the first catches an opponent unready.

rites.name: Reontor
rites.text: A low, ground-hugging technique that a wandering scholar uses to sweep an opponent off their feet during a contest of arms.

rites.name: Tiror
rites.text: A swordsman steps forward and slices downward in one quick stroke that cannot be blocked. Holding back before striking lets the blow grow stronger, and a fully charged strike sends smoke rising from the blade.

rites.name: Viases
rites.text: A fighter's repeated rapid punch sequence that once continued without end and is now capped at a few blows. It can finish off a foe pinned against a wall and can flow into a sidestep evasion.

rites.name: Nasilor
rites.text: A tumbling, staggering kick favored by one fighter in a long-running brawling contest. It has been used since the fifth installment of the competition.

rites.name: Lanes
rites.text: A near-unstoppable strike that cannot be guarded against, passed between several fighters across successive tournaments. One of its wielders also lends it to a shadowed alternate self.

rites.name: Amernes
rites.text: A reeling sway that drops its user into a feigned slump, mending a few points of wounds as they lie still. It is a technique passed among brawlers who rely on looking defeated.

rites.name: Tiallanum
rites.text: A swift grappling hurl where a fighter spins the opponent in a circle before flinging them down. A quick flick of the controls can empower it, and the crowd roars when it lands at full strength.

rites.name: Niasor
rites.text: A paired striking technique in which a fighter uses two knee strikes in succession. A later, more elaborate move is modeled on it.

rites.name: Oraurum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a warrior lands two rapid blows to the torso in quick succession. It is favored by a single brawler who has carried it since first appearing in combat.

rites.name: Miasauntum
rites.text: A fighting technique a warrior performs by sweeping a heel down onto an opponent, which can flow into a second stance. Another fighter can perform it too, and missing with it costs that user a portion of their vitality.

rites.name: Verum
rites.text: A quick forward strike that drives the palm into the foe's midsection. A fighter from the wandering folk uses it in ring contests and duels.

rites.name: Rillor
rites.text: A crouching striker technique used by a sorceress-warrior who can shift into a sharp, hunched stance mid-attack. Landing it while the foe is already reeling forces them onto the ground.

rites.name: Rernes
rites.text: A stance-based technique first practiced by a fighter in one tournament and later adopted by another. It is performed from a forward-facing starting position.

rites.name: Telosia
rites.text: A ranked technique that cannot be blocked, performed by a hunter who has used it since debuting in a tournament. A later master of the same craft also wields it.

rites.name: Valasus
rites.text: A fighter's signature finishing technique that can be redirected mid-strike. Pressing a guard or evasion input on the final blow pulls the attack back into a poised stance.

rites.name: Amiliarnium
rites.text: A fighting technique used by a gambling-minded duelist since her first appearance in a brawling tournament. It is a spinning double grapple that catches opponents off guard.

rites.name: Amonia
rites.text: A bounding strike a brawler performs from a crouched hunting posture. Its empowered form grants brief immunity and sends a foe rebounding off a barrier, and it can be charged into a grand finishing technique.

rites.name: Tollentum
rites.text: A defensive technique in which a fighter braces to absorb an incoming blow, then strikes back by stunning the foe and summoning a fierce beast ally.

rites.name: Ventus
rites.text: A masked duelist leaps skyward and spins a blade with a mechanical limb, gliding briefly before plunging down into a sudden cutting strike. Holding the descent longer makes the blow hit harder.

rites.name: Rollum
rites.text: A combat technique where a fighter spins into a rapid strike sequence. Its second blow ignites a surge of fierce momentum, and a radiant warrior form can also unleash it.

rites.name: Larnenor
rites.text: A fiery rising strike that one fighter performs to shift their stance into a blazing, wing-like posture. In certain later contests the blow also seizes the opponent in a binding snare.

rites.name: Miallum
rites.text: A ferocious bellowing technique passed down through a line of fighters, unleashed to empower the wielder's assault. In the latest iteration it ignites a surge of heightened combat fury.

rites.name: Reoniantor
rites.text: A grim technique of unstoppable force wielded by one fighter since her debut in a sparring hall. It cannot be blocked and strikes with dark, rippling energy.

rites.name: Liaria
rites.text: A grim war-cry technique practiced by a hardened commander. It extends an older roar into a repeated, sustained burst.

rites.name: Amaureornes
rites.text: A dark thrusting technique wielded by a masked warrior-king, mastered in the later era of a rival fighting tradition. It is a signature strike drawn from the shadowed arts of combat.

rites.name: Larnium
rites.text: A guarded maneuver used by a fighter who channels a dark inner power when paired with an elder ally. It lets the wielder briefly unleash special follow-up strikes, and was later replaced by a steadier stance.

rites.name: Tosteorum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a warrior drives both knees upward in rapid succession. It is favored by a single brawler who has used it since first entering the arena.

rites.name: Meontiarnum
rites.text: A fighter's aerial striking technique passed down through a lineage of combatants. A descendant can learn and perform the same rising leap in later tournaments.

rites.name: Oriasirum
rites.text: A tricky strike made with a short blade, performed by a wandering duelist. It is a technique that switches the attacker's position mid-motion to confuse the opponent.

rites.name: Coronia
rites.text: A grappling maneuver passed between several combatants across successive contests. It is a throw technique that a few fighters have learned and used over time.

rites.name: Virnor
rites.text: A fighting posture used by a wandering duelist that lets the user leap clear of low and special sweeping strikes. Its effect was later refined so the leap triggers automatically against most ground attacks.

rites.name: Amasenor
rites.text: A coiled technique performed by a fighter in a team bout, where a second strike can be queued in advance by a partner. Its follow-up blow may be readied through a teammate's timing.

rites.name: Lerus
rites.text: A grappling technique passed between fighters in a duelling circle. It can be taught to a student or claimed by a rival, and it sometimes replaces a flame-based hold when used against kin.

rites.name: Seraulor
rites.text: A swift strike that begins with a quick spring and ends in a low sweeping kick aimed at the opponent's left leg. Once a favored technique of a skilled fighter, it was later dropped from the art.

rites.name: Vaurus
rites.text: A mocking gesture performed by a fighter to provoke an opponent, shared across generations of combatants. It can be interrupted at any moment by a strike or a step.

rites.name: Lerium
rites.text: A fighter's combat technique in which a sudden lunging thrust leads into a swift sweeping strike. It is practiced by a single warrior who has mastered its rhythm.

rites.name: Nonirium
rites.text: A spinning leg strike performed by a warrior in a team combat contest. It is a technique known among the fighters of that tournament circuit.

rites.name: Cauranum
rites.text: A tumbling maneuver where a fighter drops from a standing position into an inverted balance on their hands. Two combatants have long relied on this technique in the arena.

rites.name: Sernillanum
rites.text: A brutal throwing maneuver favored by a hard-edged brawler, who uses it in place of an older heavy hurl. It forces the opponent's neck into a crushing angle.

rites.name: Cinteolum
rites.text: A combat maneuver practiced by a warrior of a distant duelist school. It is performed in close quarters to seize an opponent in a binding grip.

rites.name: Larnistum
rites.text: A fighting technique passed to a young warrior who later gains a darker form that also wields it. The technique is eventually lost from the art.

rites.name: Tianeostium
rites.text: A silent technique of unstoppable strikes wielded by a single named warrior. It has been practiced since a later era of the cycle of battles.

rites.name: Siantanum
rites.text: A heavy technique in which a fighter lifts the whole frame and slams it down onto an opponent. It is performed by a brawler known for raw strength.

rites.name: Seriasintum
rites.text: A signature technique wielded by a shadowy fighter, learned by a second practitioner after her debut. It is passed along as a prized combat art among rival duelists.

rites.name: Valares
rites.text: A two-strike technique favored by a masked brawler, where the second blow forces the foe into a helpless slump. It appears in the later fighting rounds of the arena.

rites.name: Saurornium
rites.text: A paired grappling technique in which a fighter seizes an opponent twice in rapid succession, throwing them with the second grip. It is taught to skilled practitioners of a single disciplined lineage.

rites.name: Nosum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver where a fighter hoists a foe overhead and drives them down onto the ground. It is shared among several brawlers and performed by a few named wrestlers.

rites.name: Saulium
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a combatant lands a sudden kick after the foe has been struck. The move is carried by one fighter in a long-running martial contest.

rites.name: Oranosia
rites.text: A striking sequence where a warrior drives a raised knee upward into an opponent. It is favored by a masked fighter who first used it in a later bout of an ancient arena contest.

rites.name: Raurnium
rites.text: A combat maneuver where a fighter strikes an opponent and then pivots to face away, entered by pressing a single button. It is performed by a particular fighter in a team-based arena contest.

rites.name: Lirentum
rites.text: A two-hit strike where a low jab is followed by a rising kick. If the first blow is guarded low, the second always lands, but a standing guard can stop the opening jab in later versions.

rites.name: Lostia
rites.text: A single, forceful strike favored by one fighter within an arena combat tradition. It is a signature move that marks the warrior who has trained to use it since first entering the ring.

rites.name: Teliaria
rites.text: A fighting technique passed down by a single practitioner who has used it since the earliest team contests. It is a coordinated combination of strikes performed by one fighter.

rites.name: Virneolus
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a combatant grips a carried weapon and strikes foes with it. The move is used by a single warrior in a card-based contest of skill.

rites.name: Meostus
rites.text: A standing high kick used by most fighters in the arena, which lifts an opponent into the air when it lands at the right moment. It is quick to recover and costs little, but a few fighting schools never use it.

rites.name: Seriantus
rites.text: A fighter's practiced sweeping strike, learned by two related combatants across successive tournaments. It is a technique passed from one practitioner to another.

rites.name: Nenosia
rites.text: A fighter's practiced technique that sends low-crouching rivals toppling and can strike those already fallen. In team bouts it becomes that fighter's signature joint maneuver.

rites.name: Siallia
rites.text: A grappling maneuver where a fighter traps an opponent's head in a clamp and strikes. Several duelists of one lineage learned it, and a later master replaced it with a spinning hurl.

rites.name: Nornia
rites.text: A practiced technique that a single fighter has used since first appearing in an old arena contest. It opens a brief moment in which an incoming blow can be turned aside.

rites.name: Teonastes
rites.text: A piercing knee strike that leads into a follow-up slash, performed by a fierce warrior and her monstrous transformed self. The second blow sets off a spinning twist.

rites.name: Coresus Mauranum
rites.text: A close-range striking technique in which a fighter drives their hip into an opponent. Two named combatants have relied on it across several contests.

rites.name: Mantanum
rites.text: A fighter leaps over a foe and strikes downward at low height. The leap can angle away or forward, and a delayed version can be timed for later.

rites.name: Vaurilia
rites.text: A low leg strike favored by several masked wrestlers across rival eras of the arena. If it fails to land, the fighter is left sprawled on the floor.

rites.name: Loniasor
rites.text: A deadly strike technique used by a fighter, in which the follow-up blow may be held back for a moment before landing.

rites.name: Serolum
rites.text: A combat maneuver where a fighter drives a shoulder forward and then surges upward with a rising strike. It can be queued in advance during a partner's turn, so it lands cleanly when called.

rites.name: Orianteolus
rites.text: A grappling-style maneuver a fighter performs in the arena, swapped in for an older throw that once served the same purpose.

rites.name: Meostor
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a warrior drives a heavy overhead strike downward, then slips into a fluid sidestep. A practitioner has used it since a particular tournament clash in the wider league.

rites.name: Laureostium
rites.text: A fighter's inverted balancing posture, used by several practitioners across their careers. When held idle for too long, the stance slips into a darker, mirrored form.

rites.name: Niallor
rites.text: A low-striking technique shared among several fighters since the earliest bouts. Its variants were renamed and sped up over time, and a sibling form is used by a pair of sisters.

rites.name: Oreonia
rites.text: A fighter's strike aimed at the midsection from a left-leaning stance, once a staple technique that was later dropped from the repertoire. A rougher offshoot of the same motion carries a harsher name among practitioners.

rites.name: Celiarnium
rites.text: A forward kick aimed from the off-balance side that leaves the striker shifted into a guarded readying posture. It can be delayed to chain in with a partner's attack, and it serves as a fire-up move in certain contests.

rites.name: Teleranum
rites.text: A close-range striking technique delivered with the point of the arm. It was used by a fighter in an earlier contest before being swapped out for a crouching variant.

rites.name: Vaunteonia
rites.text: A fighter rolls over the head and springs up into an upright inverted stance. Two combatants in this world have learned it as a signature technique.

rites.name: Selanum
rites.text: A fighter's strike that twists the body upward and into a spinning drop. Practitioners can start it with more than one directional input, and it has been used by a single warrior since an earlier contest.

rites.name: Malauntor
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a lone warrior unleashes a whirling storm of strikes, performed by a wandering brawler in later combat tales.

rites.name: Nentium
rites.text: A fighter's chained strike used only in one early version of a training arena's trial. Its second blow passes harmlessly over smaller crouching foes, and later revisions removed it entirely.

rites.name: Lernor
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a combatant sends a sharp upward strike through the opponent's guard, passed down between generations of twin duelists. It has been a staple of their style since the earliest days of the art.

rites.name: Serastanum
rites.text: A fighter's raised-knee strike that a combatant uses in close quarters. It has been a signature technique for one brawler since first appearing in the arena.

rites.name: Valeolanum
rites.text: A fighter shifts into a coiled stance, then strikes with a sudden twisting motion. The move is used by a nimble warrior while in that coiled posture.

rites.name: Corirnium
rites.text: A low defensive deflection technique practiced by a skilled fighter, which she has used since her first appearance. Another practitioner has also learned to perform it in later years.

rites.name: Tenanum
rites.text: A close-range striking technique in which a fighter drives the knee upward into an opponent. It is named differently depending on the region where it is taught.

rites.name: Nerus
rites.text: A low, forward-driving strike used by three fighters across all of their bouts. It is a signature technique that marks each of them as a practitioner of the same disciplined art.

rites.name: Seraustium
rites.text: A fighter's technique in which a short, blade-like weapon is driven forward in a thrust. It is used by a certain warrior who has practiced it since first appearing in a rebellion.

rites.name: Tolaurnus
rites.text: A leaping overhead strike delivered by a brawler who has used it since first entering the arena. Earlier fighters knew the same blow under a heavier, plainer name before the title was changed.

rites.name: Coraurnelum
rites.text: A low leftward strike used by a combatant from a fighting style, adopted in a later stage of a long-running contest. It launches the opponent into a quick pair of follow-up blows.

rites.name: Ceosium
rites.text: A deadly lunging technique favored by a veteran armored fighter since his first appearance in a famous combat tournament. It targets the throat with a sudden forward thrust.

rites.name: Amisaunor
rites.text: A leaping stomp technique practiced by a fighter, passed to a younger practitioner who later revives it in a later contest.

rites.name: Oronalum
rites.text: A close-quarters strike technique passed between two fighters over successive generations. It was later replaced by a different kick in a newer era of combat.

rites.name: Coriallanum
rites.text: A two-pronged strike performed by a warrior who mastered it in a recent age. It is an altered form of an older forward thrust.

rites.name: Caullonor
rites.text: A practiced maneuver favored by one fighter in a long-running arena contest. It is a striking technique that has been used by that warrior since a later round of the rivalry.

rites.name: Vantellia
rites.text: A fighter hovers aloft in a rare posture, using a blade spun like a rotor to keep themselves suspended in the air. It is a technique practiced by one famed swordsman.

rites.name: Sinosium
rites.text: A piercing forward strike performed by a masked duelist, first learned during an early contest and later passed on to a mentor. It is a kicking technique that has been part of the fighter's repertoire ever since.

rites.name: Seristor
rites.text: A combat discipline devised by a strongman for his trained bears. It is taught as a technique suited to animals rather than to people.

rites.name: Corenoria
rites.text: A close-quarters strike thrown with the rear arm, which turns into its mirror image when begun from the opposite stance. It belongs to a fighter's repertoire of martial strikes.

rites.name: Telenia
rites.text: A close-quarters charge in which a fighter drops the shoulder and drives into an opponent's lower body. It is a move used by a certain brawler in a tag-team arena contest.

rites.name: Silus Nianium
rites.text: A two-handed thrust technique used by a single warrior, first shown in a recent tournament-era duel. It is performed as part of a larger sequence of strikes called Heaven and Earth.

rites.name: Sereolles
rites.text: A deceptive fighting maneuver that a single wandering blade-master has used across several generations of contests. Later followers renamed it, and it is still practiced today.

rites.name: Teliantanus
rites.text: A combat technique where a fighter swings a hook, drives the body forward into a thrust, then whips back with a reversed chopping strike. A particular warrior has long favored it since first appearing in a major tournament.

rites.name: Niases
rites.text: A practiced maneuver used by two fighters who have returned to the contest. Landing it also causes a restraining snare to form around the opponent.

rites.name: Amostium Sereolor
rites.text: A fighting posture used by two combatants that opens the way to follow-up strikes. In a later version the posture becomes a lasting state entered after a particular blow.

rites.name: Naurneollus
rites.text: A bound-together strike technique practiced by two fighters that can be queued while a partner is still acting. It returns from a long absence.

rites.name: Corum
rites.text: A ritual maneuver practiced by a wandering seeker of the workshop guilds. Once invoked, it binds the fervor of the practitioner and ignites a sudden surge of inner heat.

rites.name: Corilum
rites.text: A silent striking technique practiced by a masked mentor of crows. It delivers a hidden venom through a thin hooked point, a method learned in the later age of the guild.

rites.name: Oreontium
rites.text: A grappling technique practiced by a wandering duelist, one that delivers a heavy crushing blow. Since its first appearance it has been counted among the forceful strikes that cannot be interrupted once started.

rites.name: Cillium
rites.text: A rapid string of open-palm strikes delivered by a warrior who spins mid-combo. Its final blow leaves the striker reeling and unsteady, though it can be linked into a kicking sequence.

rites.name: Ralanum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a combatant performs two rapid spinning kicks in succession. A master of a certain martial style has used it for years in competitive bouts.

rites.name: Coriarnum
rites.text: A striking sequence that a fighter once used in a duel, a technique later dropped from the training of later generations.

rites.name: Collaustor
