rites.text: A low, deceptive fighting technique that a rogue duelist uses to mislead an opponent before striking. A mentor of the craft later learns and teaches the same maneuver.

rites.name: Nesium
rites.text: A combat technique used by a sword-wielding wanderer that, when a specific input follows the opening strike, shifts into a different stance. The follow-up blow lands weaker if the wielder is in a particular heightened state.

rites.name: Coreonalium
rites.text: A swift, layered strike performed by a fighter in a team bout of arena combat. It is one of the named techniques a warrior uses to trap an opponent.

rites.name: Meosia Amaulor
rites.text: A grappling throw in which the wielder hurls a foe overhead, then drops onto the fallen body. It can be chained into a follow-up limb-wrenching hold.

rites.name: Sereoraulia
rites.text: A fighter's aerial striking technique in which the body rotates backward mid-air to deliver a kick. It has been adopted by a pair of rival warriors across separate tournaments.

rites.name: Oresia
rites.text: A grappling technique favored by a wiry brawler who has used it since first entering the arena. It hooks an opponent and drags them into a hard, close-quarters throw.

rites.name: Tialistor
rites.text: A swift strike used by a wandering blade-master since the earliest days of the arena. When cast during a charged stance it reaches less far, and in later iterations that stance knocks foes into a stumbling bound.

rites.name: Tausanum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver used by a fighter across several bouts. A darker form of the same hold is also known to be used by a second, more savage version of that fighter.

rites.name: Linauror
rites.text: A ranged hooking maneuver used by a towering brawler in combat, where the attacker snares an opponent and then unleashes an empowered heat-fueled strike.

rites.name: Senor
rites.text: A fighting technique used by a martial artist in later bouts of a combat contest. Its second strike can cause the opponent to be pinned in place for a moment.

rites.name: Laustirnia
rites.text: A fighter's striking sequence begins with a rear-leg kick and flows into a shift onto the opposite footing. It was a signature technique of one combatant for many years before being dropped from later editions of the art.

rites.name: Caulles
rites.text: A sinuous fighting technique practiced by two linked duelists who share a family line. It is performed in tag combat, and one of the pair can also carry it into later bouts.

rites.name: Amirnium
rites.text: A fighting maneuver where a warrior lunges forward and then sweeps the legs of an opponent low. It was once used by a famous brawler but was later dropped from his repertoire.

rites.name: Neornoses
rites.text: A fighter's rapid two-blow sequence that is quicker than the standard version of the same attack. It deals greater harm, though at first it looks identical to the slower form.

rites.name: Valaulor Nantaustes
rites.text: A practiced maneuver used by a fighter ever since her first appearance in a grand arena contest. It is a set technique in her repertoire of combat moves.

rites.name: Seonus Amiallia
rites.text: A fighter's chained technique in which a rapid sequence of blows ends in a sweeping arc of the blade. It was once a signature sequence of a particular duelist before being dropped from later training.

rites.name: Ventanum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver where a fighter lifts a rival from behind and hurls them backward onto the floor. It is performed by a masked warrior and passed to a successor in later bouts.

rites.name: Vornanum
rites.text: A grappling technique where a fighter seizes a foe from behind and hurls them over the shoulder. It overrides ordinary seizes when used on a rear-facing opponent, though a few special maneuvers still take priority over it.

rites.name: Venanum Rernases
rites.text: A fighter's technique in which two quick blows are delivered in sequence, a left followed by a right. It is a personal variant of a common paired-strike form, first used when the fighter entered the arena.

rites.name: Riantostium
rites.text: A grappling hold in which a wrestler lifts a foe and drives them headfirst into the ground. Several defenders can break free of it mid-air, and certain fighters are the only ones trained to use it.

rites.name: Tistum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver in which a fighter seizes an opponent and reverses their momentum into a locked hold. It is favored by a brawler who has used it since first appearing in a tournament.

rites.name: Amaustor
rites.text: A combat maneuver favored by a fighter who first appeared in a later battle tournament. The technique is carried by a single warrior and remains a signature move in her arsenal.

rites.name: Tollantia
rites.text: A rapid sweeping leg technique favored by one martial artist since the second great tournament. It strikes low and fast, catching opponents off guard.

rites.name: Sauntium
rites.text: A three-part maneuver that a fighter performs in close combat, linked to a particular combatant who uses it in the arena. It has been part of that fighter's repertoire since the sixth round of the contests.

rites.name: Vosiallia
rites.text: A hidden sweeping maneuver performed in a cursed bearing, where the user spins low and strikes the foe's legs. Its later form spares the user from self-harm, and it never leaves the opponent reeling when blocked.

rites.name: Mintenes
rites.text: A swift strike technique favored by a pair of fighters who have trained in it for years. A veteran brawler also returns to use it in a later tournament.

rites.name: Telestanes
rites.text: A fighting technique performed by a single warrior in an arena duel. A later revision of the technique divides it into two separate strikes.

rites.name: Leorninus
rites.text: A raised leg swings downward in a crushing arc onto a foe, forcing them to sink low on impact. It is the follow-up blow of a larger sweeping technique, used alone.

rites.name: Cauntostor
rites.text: A brawler's grappling shove seizes a foe from behind and drives them forward. If the foe stands against a barrier, the brawler slams them into it, opening them up for follow-up strikes.

rites.name: Nasollium
rites.text: A practiced strike technique passed down through a bloodline of fighters. It was once known by an older name and is performed by an elder and later by her descendant.

rites.name: Ranium
rites.text: A brutal open-palm strike favored by a sharp-tempered tinkerer during tag bouts. It lands with a sudden, ringing force that rattles the opponent.

rites.name: Oraullor
rites.text: A hidden technique of a wandering assassin that delivers a tiny tainted barb through a quick strike. It has been passed among the practitioners of this craft and then taught to a masterful student.

rites.name: Lases
rites.text: A swift fighting technique used by a skilled duelist that can be repeated against a foe struck from behind near a barrier. The barrier cancels recoil, so the blows can be chained until the opponent turns back around.

rites.name: Silernanum
rites.text: A fighter's rapid two-step striking technique, a near copy of a longer combination minus its final blow. It has been practiced by one combatant since the earliest days of the training grounds.

rites.name: Seoneria
rites.text: A swift arcing strike performed by a fighter of a rival lineage, learned in a later contest. A companion of that same trial was also able to perform it.

rites.name: Amentanum Niasteorium
rites.text: A practiced striking technique used by one fighter within a sparring tradition. It has been performed since the third great contest of the arena circuit.

rites.name: Rosum
rites.text: A forceful blow thrown straight ahead by a brawler who has trained it for years. In later contests it can crush an opponent's guard and stagger them.

rites.name: Vasium
rites.text: A hidden technique in which a wielder spins a toxin-coated blade to strike foes. It can also be unleashed from a stance of pure focus, though with a shorter reach.

rites.name: Ceontum
rites.text: A bodily stance adopted by a warrior in combat, used to shift weight and position during a fight. It is practiced by one named fighter of the arena.

rites.name: Nirium
rites.text: A hidden grappling technique known only to a single wielder, used in a small number of ancient tournament contests. It lets a fighter hurl an opponent to the ground in a sudden, unexpected move.

rites.name: Ameontia
rites.text: A two-strike technique that a fighter can use from the start of their career. If the first blow is blocked, the second still arrives unless the defender sidesteps or retreats quickly to avoid it.

rites.name: Mentium
rites.text: A rhythmic strike technique practiced by one warrior, first used in a later contest of skill. The strike is performed with a rolling, booming motion.

rites.name: Valarnisor
rites.text: A grappling hold used by a masked wrestler that follows a heel lock and ends a bout. If the opponent slips free, they kick the wrestler away and take a small wound.

rites.name: Veosia Riarnes
rites.text: A two-stage striking technique performed by a pair of martial practitioners. The final blow can be held back and delayed before it lands.

rites.name: Rinus Orastor
rites.text: A fighter's technique of swinging the weapon's grip end in a wide arc to batter an opponent. A veteran warrior has practiced it for years in tournament bouts.

rites.name: Lenus
rites.text: A practiced strike technique that a fighter can enter by pressing two buttons after an opening blow. Its follow-up can be held back briefly, and its reach shrinks when used during a heightened stance.

rites.name: Caustornum
rites.text: A combined strike technique that a wandering duelist first performs in a later era of training. Later, a master of the same discipline learns to use it as well.

rites.name: Reosiantum
rites.text: A practiced strike that cannot be defended against, used by a fighter in a team contest. It takes the place of an older unavoidable technique the same fighter once relied on.

rites.name: Mernus Tastus
rites.text: A practiced maneuver that a fighter performs in close combat, taken up in place of an older technique. It is favored by one skilled duelist of a northern guild.

rites.name: Saunirnor
rites.text: A timed striking technique performed by a single fighter. Halting partway through the motion leaves the fighter in a rigid, stiff-armed stance, while holding low during the final motion keeps the fighter crouched close to the ground.

rites.name: Teollaunor
rites.text: A swift defensive technique in which a fighter slips past an incoming strike and answers at once with a hand-and-fist combination. Several practitioners across generations have learned it.

rites.name: Nistus Serilor
rites.text: A three-part striking technique taught to a single fighter, where a forward press during the opening blows shifts the body into a coiled stance. Later blows then hold the fighter in a feigned stillness before ending in a sideways slither.

rites.name: Laulontus
rites.text: A fighter's acrobatic kick that flips the body backward through the air. Several training variants exist, and it can finish a chained combo sequence.

rites.name: Salornor
rites.text: A fighter's technique in which a practitioner spins across the ground to strike an opponent. It has been used by one combatant for many years.

rites.name: Cintor
rites.text: A stepping technique favored by one fighter in a long-running tag tournament, used since its earliest matches. It involves a quick sequence of footwork that unsettles opponents.

rites.name: Sollintia
rites.text: A grappling technique used by a single fighter who has relied on it across several later contests. It is a practiced hold that pins an opponent in place.

rites.name: Sirnantium
rites.text: A fighter's technique performed while holding a particular guard posture. It is used by one brawler across several bouts.

rites.name: Veolium Teonistanum
rites.text: A coiling hand technique passed down by a wandering duelist. Pressing one direction shifts the fighter into a crouched, clawed stance.

rites.name: Coronia Rauntor
rites.text: A fighting technique where a warrior strikes low with a rapid sequence of sweeping kicks. It is a signature maneuver of one particular combatant who has used it since their first public tournament appearance.

rites.name: Cauntirum
rites.text: A practiced maneuver performed by a single fighter that, once it lands, binds the opponent in a brief hold.

rites.name: Terniares
rites.text: A brutal crushing technique used by a towering war-brute in combat. When it strikes an opening at the right moment, the fighter seizes the foe and drives them forward, pinning them hard against any barrier behind them.

rites.name: Carianor
rites.text: A harmless hurling technique performed by a brawler, which opens the way for a chain of grappling follow-ups when it connects.

rites.name: Tiarnus Mellum
rites.text: A heavy, repeatable maneuver favored by a brawler named Holt, first performed in an early tournament circuit and later dropped from the fighting repertoire entirely.

rites.name: Coreonanum Tollus
rites.text: A martial technique once taught to all students of a fighting school, later lost to the lineage's masters. Its low sweep sends foes sprawling, and skilled users can chain it into a spinning kick follow-up.

rites.name: Mirnium
rites.text: A short striking sequence used by a fighter of a disciplined martial school. Pressing the second strike again extends it into a follow-up combination.

rites.name: Orauntes
rites.text: A grounding strike delivered with an open palm that drives an opponent down to the earth. It is performed by a wrestler-like fighter who has used it in later battles.

rites.name: Launes
rites.text: A fighter's technique that a single warrior has used since first appearing in the arena. It serves as one of her decisive forceful strikes that can break an opponent's guard.

rites.name: Amenollor
rites.text: A open-palmed strike favored by two sisters of a fighting tradition, used since the later rounds of their rivalry to open a flurry of retaliatory blows.

rites.name: Sereorenia
rites.text: A forceful strike practiced by a warrior of an ancient clan, the technique is performed in place of an older, plainer blow. It belongs to the fighting arts of the clan's line.

rites.name: Valentinia
rites.text: A dark sweeping technique first used by a masked fighter in an earlier contest, later passed on to a mentor's pupil in a later one. It is a learned strike move.

rites.name: Vaurnes
rites.text: A stinging open-handed strike favored by a wandering dancer in the arena since her first appearance. It is a signature technique that marks her fighting style among rival duelists.

rites.name: Saurnor Naustia
rites.text: A swift, short thrust performed by a warrior with a blade. It is a quick attack that strikes an opponent before they can respond.

rites.name: Callanum Tonia
rites.text: A swift strike delivered with the rear leg, favored by a wandering duelist. It was first shown in a tournament of raw combatants.

rites.name: Coreostus Valornus
rites.text: A charging elbow-and-arm technique that fighters unleash after sprinting several strides. When it lands on an alert opponent, the foe is flung rolling across the ground.

rites.name: Laulanum
rites.text: A fighting maneuver favored by one warrior, in which the practitioner steps forward on the right foot with a sudden lunging motion. It has been used in contests since the earliest arena tournaments.

rites.name: Nones
rites.text: A fighter's technique in which a heeled strike is delivered while spinning rightward, adopted by one warrior in a later contest to replace an earlier sweeping kick.

rites.name: Canes Rileorum
rites.text: A fighting technique practiced by a warrior and later taught to her child. It is used in later contests of skill and combat.

rites.name: Sonallanum
rites.text: A recoiling strike that a warrior can unleash only while wearing a darkened guise, hitting harder than a standard thrust but harming the striker too. Its partner in the guise can chain it into a powerful finishing sequence.

rites.name: Oriallia
rites.text: A grappling technique in which a fighter locks an opponent's leg, then pins the head in a choke. If the victim slips free, they kick back and strike their captor.

rites.name: Telonauntor
rites.text: A swift strike favored by two wandering duelists, once nameless and later given a title. In later practice it tracks its target and can set off a spinning twist.

rites.name: Niallia
rites.text: A fighter's signature strike that a warrior unleashes in several forms across different eras. It is passed from a human warrior to his darker alter ego, and can be used again in a later climactic duel.

rites.name: Caustanum
rites.text: A evasive fighting technique used by a warrior from her first appearance in the arena, taking the place of a counter maneuver during a surge of power.

rites.name: Naustelles
rites.text: A fighter's combat technique that begins with a driving downward blow and finishes with a rising punch. Some versions allow a partner to step in and complete the final strike.

rites.name: Lentiarum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a practitioner seizes an opponent and drives them down with a sudden lunging strike. It belongs to one performer of the craft and is named in a separate entry for another performer's version.

rites.name: Niaronus
rites.text: A coordinated volley of rapid strikes launched in quick succession by a single fighter. It was first used by a warrior who entered the arena in a later age of the contest.

rites.name: Amelliantus
rites.text: A fighter's technique that hurls a cloud of grit into an opponent's face. After it lands, the user can slip into a silent sidestep by pressing down and forward.

rites.name: Amolium
rites.text: A swift striking technique in which a fighter pivots and snaps a high reverse punch with the left arm. It is practiced by one particular combatant who has used it since first entering the arena.

rites.name: Valeoria Amarnaules
rites.text: A violent maneuver a fighter uses in a tournament bout, performed by one combatant in a brawling contest of two-person teams.

rites.name: Loseornor
rites.text: A fighter dashes forward and launches into a flying kick that leaves the attacker sprawled on the ground. When it lands cleanly up close, it can lock the foe's leg for a follow-up hold.

rites.name: Seraliria
rites.text: A maneuver that a single fighter can execute only while a reflected double stands beside them. Once introduced, a practitioner can recover while facing forward by pressing the forward input.

rites.name: Telesaurnum
rites.text: A coiling wrestling technique that a fighter uses to lock an opponent in a crushing embrace. Another brawler known for brute strength has also learned to perform it.

rites.name: Amestires
rites.text: A grappling technique in which one fighter seizes an opponent and hurls them to the ground. It is used by three related combatants across several contests.

rites.name: Rolerus
rites.text: A throwing technique used by two sisters since the earliest days of the bout, which one of them later loses. A heavy brawler once shared it, but he forgot the move in later rounds.

rites.name: Tistum Lasium
rites.text: A fighter's strike sequence of two quick blows followed by a middle kick, passed down by one practitioner across several bouts. It was later set aside in favor of a whirling leg technique.

rites.name: Nilanum
rites.text: A swift technique in which a fighter unleashes a quick flurry of blows before slipping away unseen. It belongs to a single warrior's repertoire.

rites.name: Riarnausium
rites.text: A striking technique that a single practitioner has used for years. It resembles an airborne kick used by a rival school.

rites.name: Kalusarlaum
rites.text: Kalusarlaum is the concept of the Walled Age in Brurnadeld, the long stretch in which peoples raised holding walls and built orders and churches around their hearths. It is felt in the patience of masons and in the first crossings made where walls at last met open ground. Its power lies less in blows than in the enduring shape it gives to every place it touches.

rites.name: Ameosanum
rites.text: A recognised technique of combat performed by a single fighter in a modern arena contest. It is executed with a sequence of strikes that scatter an opponent's guard.

rites.name: Manteolanum
rites.text: A warrior unleashes a relentless, unstoppable strike that no defense can block. It is performed by a fighter in a tournament of an early modern age arena contest.

rites.name: Rianteollum
rites.text: A tumbling kick technique used by two related fighters across many contests. In a tag-style bout the follow-up blow can be queued by a partner, and a shift into a rising spinning strike is possible during the opening blow.

rites.name: Vanentia
rites.text: A coordinated attack performed by a fighter and her demonic counterpart, sharing one technique. It is a single maneuver executed by two linked combatants.

rites.name: Raullum
rites.text: A practiced maneuver that a cunning doctor has used for years, flipping the body backward in a quick, acrobatic motion to unsettle opponents.

rites.name: Sianus
rites.text: A fighter's chained strike that a skilled practitioner can extend into a longer barrage. Its second blow may be held back before landing, and it draws on a related technique.

rites.name: Cenes
rites.text: A short striking technique used by a fighter in a tournament. It is a move that strikes with the elbow in a dropping motion.

rites.name: Millus
rites.text: A ranged strike technique wielded by a line of mechanical sentinels, passed through successive generations of their kind. One early model in the line was denied the technique until much later.

rites.name: Sereles
rites.text: A deceptive striking tactic in which a fighter pretends to aim high before quickly driving a blow into the opponent's torso. It is employed by a brawler from a modern combat tournament.

rites.name: Neontalum
rites.text: A high-kicking stance-shifting technique used by a single fighter since their debut in a tournament-era combat contest. It lets the practitioner rock sideways while striking from an unusual angle.

rites.name: Canium
rites.text: A recurring hurling maneuver practiced by a traveling duelist, which replaces a familiar strike once known as the Mad Axes. It is a technique passed among fighters who contest in tag matches.

rites.name: Amalaurnus
rites.text: A fighter's rapid two-step technique that a single warrior has used since first appearing in a combat tournament. It is a flowing combination strike that bursts forward in quick succession.

rites.name: Riastus
rites.text: A signature technique wielded by one fighter in a modern combat arena. It is a move the warrior has relied on since first stepping into the ring.

rites.name: Valenium
rites.text: A quick sidestep followed by a cutting strike, favored by a warrior of the modern age. It is a technique passed down among fighters who train in the arena.

rites.name: Amiantus
rites.text: A technique wielded by a fighter ever since her debut in a competitive arena. It is a rolling, undulating strike that carries a dark, pulsing momentum through an opponent's guard.

rites.name: Nialus
rites.text: A fighter's sidestep technique is performed by a young combatant who has used it since first entering a sanctioned tournament. It is a defensive footwork maneuver known for its quick lateral evasion.

rites.name: Valeostor
rites.text: A practiced combat technique used by a single fighter since first appearing in a recent tournament arena. It delivers a sudden blow that its wielder favors in close bouts.

rites.name: Sillia
rites.text: A fighter's technique that strikes twice in quick succession, where the second blow can bind an opponent in place. In some arenas the opening strike can also be queued during a partner's turn.

rites.name: Vornauntes
rites.text: A crossing blow favored by a sword-bearing warlord in the later campaigns. It is a technique practiced in modern duels to strike an opponent from an unexpected angle.

rites.name: Sintia
rites.text: A paired strike technique used by a single fighter, where the second blow lands in quick succession after the first. In some tournament versions the follow-up hit can trap the opponent in a binding state.

rites.name: Corisanum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a practitioner links a sweeping leg attack into a rising follow-up. It is taught to one particular combatant and has been used by her in recent contests.

rites.name: Valorentium
rites.text: A fighter's technique that replaces two of his older sequences of ten strikes. It appears in the newest version of the contest and follows a removed sequence from earlier editions.

rites.name: Amaustantes
rites.text: A evasive fighting technique in which a combatant drops low and slips past an incoming strike. It leaves the opponent toppled to the ground and open to a sustained follow-up assault.

rites.name: Corilles
rites.text: A striking technique that a pair of fighters can unleash, one in their mortal guise and one in their demonic guise. It is a move used in combat by these two forms of the same wielder.

rites.name: Rerium
rites.text: A bursting flurry of blossoming frost that a fighter unleashes as a single heated finishing technique. It is the decisive strike a combatant saves for the peak of a battle.

rites.name: Seonausum
rites.text: A swift striking technique used by a physician-fighter in a tournament of paired combatants. It is performed while an opponent is pinned under a rain of blows.

rites.name: Tianteosia
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a combatant drives an opponent into searing heat while fastened in a sworn bond. It is performed by a practitioner of an advanced warrior school.

rites.name: Vollirnus
rites.text: A forceful downward strike unleashed by a fighter in a heated, enraged state. It is one of two heat-fueled finishing blows available to its wielder.

rites.name: Valileres
rites.text: A forceful striking technique performed with the upper body, used by a towering warrior since first appearing in a famous combat tournament saga.

rites.name: Serirnania
rites.text: A sweeping low strike performed by a fighter with a mechanical hand, used since the fighter first entered a major contest. It is one of the signature techniques of this combatant.

rites.name: Corintus
rites.text: A fighter drops low and then springs upward with a knee strike that launches the opponent into the air. A practitioner has used this technique for many years, and a later variant borrows its form.

rites.name: Siaraulia
rites.text: A fighting technique used by a brawler who first appeared in a recent combat tournament. It is a kick that the fighter relies on in battle.

rites.name: Oreontum
rites.text: A practiced courtesy-based maneuver used by a fighter in a combat arena. It works as a deceptive move that draws opponents into a false sense of security.

rites.name: Ceonanum
rites.text: A rapid open-hand technique used by a winged fighter in a team combat tournament. It strikes an opponent with a swift palm attack.

rites.name: Veoronus
rites.text: A fighter's technique of rapid, looping kicks delivered in midair while closing distance. Some practitioners delay the final strike, while others repurpose the motion in different combat styles.

rites.name: Saurus
rites.text: A spinning strike used by a rugged mechanical fighter that can lift a foe into the air and twist them about. When it lands cleanly, it spins the opponent and sends them flying away.

rites.name: Ameontauses
rites.text: A close-quarters striking technique in which the fighter drives the point of the arm into an opponent. It is used by one fighter in an early contest and later appears as the finishing strike of a longer combination for another.

rites.name: Lonus
rites.text: A fighter's signature sequence of strikes has been passed down through years of bouts. Later performers adapt its ending into their own finishing combinations.

rites.name: Veones
rites.text: A spinning strike technique used by a mechanical fighter across several generations, later retired in favor of a new maneuver. Its motion survives as part of a stronger combo finisher.

rites.name: Rarnillanum
rites.text: A fighting technique favored by a brawler who first took to the ring in a later tournament. It is a sidestepping maneuver used by one combatant since their introduction.

rites.name: Varornes
rites.text: A brawler's chained assault that a hulking fighter performs from the fifth bout onward. It is known by a different name in the region where it originated.

rites.name: Telarnium
rites.text: A combat technique a fighter unlocks, letting them shift into a violent, ruinous stance. Its final strike can set off a spiraling twist that tears at the opponent.

rites.name: Sones
rites.text: A grappling maneuver used by a single fighter, which can be countered within a narrower timing window than most similar holds. Its timing was later adjusted to be harder to escape.

rites.name: Valilus
rites.text: A fighting technique wielded by a single named combatant who first displayed it in a recent tournament. It is a signature blow tied to one warrior's style.

rites.name: Valeostum
rites.text: A heavy technique passed between two fighting brutes, a rolling motion that rewards a clean strike with extra force. Its power has shifted over time and was lessened in later versions.

rites.name: Lises
rites.text: A rear-footed kicking technique favored by a single fighter who learned it during her first appearance in a combat tournament. It is used as a signature strike in close-quarters bouts.

rites.name: Ternanor
rites.text: A swift forward lunge that a fighter performs in a team bout, ending in a strike that a partner can prepare in advance. It is a technique passed among warriors who train in pairs.

rites.name: Serintellor
rites.text: A nearly unavoidable strike unleashed by a masked brawler, which, when it lands at the perfect moment, cloaks the target in flames that burn only in appearance.

rites.name: Reontus
rites.text: A fighter's rising leap-kick sequence that a practitioner may end by dropping flat instead of springing upright. In a crossover contest it forms the opening strikes of a special finishing combination.

rites.name: Tiarollus
rites.text: A piercing strike that two fighters have learned over the years. A third combatant later adopted it too.

rites.name: Telantanum
rites.text: A stroke that a wielder performs with a bladed motion. When the final blow strikes an airborne foe, the wielder is lifted into a rising surge, which can be halted by a quick counter-signal.

rites.name: Seranus
rites.text: A fighting technique used by a warrior since first appearing in a clash of martial arts. It is a strike performed with the right hand.

rites.name: Lestilor
rites.text: A reactive technique used by sturdy automatons and a certain machine-maker's creation after they are struck by a fiery burst. While dazed, the user can restore a small amount of vigor, yet remains open to incoming blows during the repair.

rites.name: Telilanum
rites.text: A violent, sudden descent that a fighter performs as a signature maneuver. It has belonged to one combatant since her first appearance in the arena.

rites.name: Nisonus
rites.text: A fighting technique performed by a single practitioner, first shown in a later tournament-era combat contest. It is a striking maneuver that the same fighter uses throughout the contests they enter.

rites.name: Nonialus
rites.text: A stealthy technique wielded by a fighter since her first appearance in a combat tournament. It is a signature maneuver tied to her character.

rites.name: Corastium
rites.text: A combat technique a fighter performs with a sudden, cold reset of her stance. It appears in her early appearances and is also used by a towering brute in a later tag contest.

rites.name: Virnium
rites.text: A grappling technique in which a hulking brawler uses both arms to catch and yank an opponent inward. It has been known to a single fighter since their first appearance in combat.

rites.name: Amirus
rites.text: A practiced strike sequence that two fighters learn over the years, its final blow can be held back for a moment. In team bouts, partners may queue that closing blow ahead of time.

rites.name: Amirnanum
rites.text: A fighting posture adopted by a warrior named Varek since a later tournament. Another fighter named Ossin can also take up this same stance.

rites.name: Liarnum
rites.text: A violent maneuver used by a brawler in a fighting arena, serving as one of his fiery engagement techniques. It is delivered in a single forceful strike.

rites.name: Orestia
rites.text: A sudden airborne kick launched from a standing position, used by several fighters across generations. Some practitioners use a delayed dashing variant, and a sideways-input form that can flow into follow-up strikes or a quick roll.

rites.name: Terontanum
rites.text: A fighting technique used by one brawler across several bouts. Its opening strikes chain together neatly when the first one lands as a counter, and they lead into a later empowered variant.

rites.name: Amerninor
rites.text: A bladed combat technique in which a swordsman's opening strike is chained into a backward elbow cut, and a skilled user can continue into a rapid flurry of hooked jabs. In later forms, the second blow twists the opponent's body into a spinning throw.

rites.name: Amernia
rites.text: A fighting technique wielded by a warrior since his first appearance in a sparring hall. It can be learned by a second fighter in a transformed state, replacing another blow. Later revisions let it strike at any moment and turn into a gliding dash when a direction is held.

rites.name: Teloriales
rites.text: A fighter's rising strike performed with a sweeping, swaying motion of the leg. It is a signature technique carried by one particular combatant since a team tournament.

rites.name: Rausium
rites.text: A practiced low sweeping strike used by a fighter from the time they first entered the arena. It cuts beneath an opponent's guard.

rites.name: Verneontia
rites.text: A two-strike technique used by a wandering duelist. Holding the low guard during the first blow shifts the stance into a coiling crouch, while holding forward during the second blow shifts it into a staggering sway.

rites.name: Mialles
rites.text: A practiced maneuver favored by one fighter and taken up by a rival in later contests. Its opening motion can flow into a mirrored counter, and in team bouts a partner may queue it in advance.

rites.name: Cernum
rites.text: A combat technique in which a fighter delivers two rapid strikes aimed at the middle body. It is practiced by a single warrior and has been used since a certain tournament era.

rites.name: Seraullor
rites.text: A swift grappling technique that one fighter has used since a later rebellion-era contest. It is a move passed from one combatant to the next.

rites.name: Ameolornor
rites.text: A reversal technique in which a fighter turns a blow back on the attacker. It only works against one specific foe and triggers on its own after a successful counter strike.

rites.name: Reranum
rites.text: A piercing strike technique used by a fighter who has trained in its form since a later tournament era. It is performed with a sudden forward lunge.

rites.name: Telostirum
rites.text: A signature maneuver used by a brawler in a combat contest since its later installment. It is a technique the fighter relies on in close battle.

rites.name: Niarosia
rites.text: A practiced maneuver in which a healer-scholar of the Hollow Guild draws in a foe's exhalation and turns it against them. It is recorded in the training manuals of the southern academies.

rites.name: Rauntum
rites.text: A forward strike used by three fighters in every bout they fight. It is a signature technique that marks each combatant's style.

rites.name: Coreosia
rites.text: A signature technique performed by a wielder while in her unleashed, ruinous state. It is first shown in a rebellious bloodline contest and belongs to one particular fighter.

rites.name: Veostirnum
rites.text: A practiced technique that a single wielder uses to cancel an enchantment or spell in play. The art has been carried into the wielder's fighting style since first appearing in that user's early public contests.

rites.name: Sellor
rites.text: A fighter's final maneuver that a warrior can hold back for a moment before releasing it. Its closing strike can be deferred once it has been learned.

rites.name: Maurnum
rites.text: A bow-like gesture a fighter performs in a duel, which turns into a different strike when it lands at the right moment of an opening.

rites.name: Laurus
rites.text: A two-strike fighting technique that a warrior uses in place of an older double attack. Its second blow is said to trigger a twisting spin.

rites.name: Masaullor
rites.text: A quick close-range attack used by a fighter during tag bouts. It is a playful jab delivered with the elbow.

rites.name: Tesum
rites.text: A paired striking technique delivered with the fist of the rear hand twice in quick succession. It was once practiced by a certain fighter but later dropped from the repertoire.

rites.name: Reostanum
rites.text: A front throw in which a fighter seizes an opponent's neck and drives them down. Its style shifts over time, and it leaves the user either lying still or rising on their own.

rites.name: Amontum
rites.text: A forced technique a fighter uses to rearrange their stance mid-clash. It also works as a heat-building opener that charges up the combatant's surge.

rites.name: Corintes
rites.text: A two-strike technique performed by a single fighter in a duel. In later bouts, its second blow can cause the opponent's body to twist and spin out of control.

rites.name: Cillernium
rites.text: A fighter's signature two-blow technique that stuns the opponent after the second strike. Later refinements let the user return to a guarded stance by pressing a chosen input pair.

rites.name: Launtilor
rites.text: A practiced strike used by a warrior of a distant clan, performed during a duel of fists. It is known among combatants of this world as a technique of falling blows.

rites.name: Corillia
rites.text: A bold aerial technique performed by a well-dressed fighter during his first appearance in a combat tournament. It lets the user launch into the air with a flourish.

rites.name: Leolus
rites.text: A fighter drops into a falling heel strike and flows directly into a chaotic judgement stance. It links two fighting postures into one continuous motion.

rites.name: Tillum
rites.text: A leaping strike that drives one knee forward from the air. A fighter who has learned the art of soaring uses it to crash into an opponent with raw momentum.

rites.name: Valintia
rites.text: A forceful technique used by a seasoned fighter as a secondary surge of wrath. It was later given a formal designation and its input sequence was revised.

rites.name: Selleornor
rites.text: A defensive technique in which a fighter retreats backward and then halts the motion mid-step. It is practiced by a single martial artist who has used it in combat for years.

rites.name: Cellones
rites.text: A fighting technique wielded by one warrior in a combat arena. Its final blow wears down an opponent's guard and also kindles a surge of fierce energy for the user.

rites.name: Vianaurnum
rites.text: A practiced maneuver that a skilled fighter performs to strike an opponent who has moved. It is linked to one particular fighter and has been used by her since she first entered the arena.

rites.name: Ceonia
rites.text: A grappling maneuver where a fighter cancels a rushing dive into a lifting takedown. Its escape timing shifts with stance and range, and a grounded or distant foe takes a skull strike instead.

rites.name: Rernium
rites.text: A two-part strike where a sweeping slash is followed by a heavy blow that lifts a foe into the air. The second part can miss against a target that has been slammed to the ground.

rites.name: Neonallor
rites.text: A fighter links a heavy fist blow into a stronger follow-up strike. The second hit can be held to build force, and a held strike can crush an opponent against a barrier.

rites.name: Nelleonum
rites.text: A quick evasive maneuver favored by a certain fighter. It is performed as a fluid hopping sequence, and the technique has been used by that practitioner since their first public appearance.

rites.name: Oraurnes
rites.text: A ferocious technique wielded by a warrior of the wilds, drawing on a rolling tide of strikes. It is a signature art that marks its user's combat style.

rites.name: Vianteostus
rites.text: A heavy overhead blow favored by one fighter that can be held back before its second impact. It lands as a natural follow-up only when it catches an opponent mid-attack.

rites.name: Valaustonor
rites.text: A grappling maneuver practiced by a fighter named Kessaru Oda in a tournament arena. It is used to seize and throw an opponent within close combat.

rites.name: Corantus
rites.text: A evasive strike technique in which a fighter lowers the upper body to slip beneath an incoming attack, then drives a punch into the opponent's torso. It is favored by one particular combatant who has relied on it for many years.

rites.name: Orentus
rites.text: A fighting technique of kicks performed by one practitioner. It is known as the signature move of a single martial artist, who uses it since first stepping into the arena.

rites.name: Oraullium
rites.text: A two-sister fighting technique that starts with a quick kick chain. Its later entries can be recovered from, and its follow-up strike sometimes misses after an earlier hit.

rites.name: Teleosor
rites.text: A fighter's rapid pair of jabs that flows straight into a sweeping low kick. It is a technique passed down by one practitioner since first appearing in a combat tournament.

rites.name: Aminolia
rites.text: A swift aerial technique performed by a practiced fighter who drops low and then rises gracefully into a sweeping leap.

rites.name: Mianium
rites.text: A close-quarters strike technique in which the fighter drives a sharp elbow into an opponent's body. It is practiced by a single brawler who relies on it as a signature maneuver.

rites.name: Teleornia
rites.text: A swift spinning technique that a warrior uses to halt an attack mid-motion. It is first seen in a tournament-style fighting arena.

rites.name: Ameosor Ceollianium
rites.text: A fighter's technique is a variation within a family of rapid forward-led sequences, and in its newest form it is replaced by a related spinning maneuver.

rites.name: Talonium
rites.text: A fighting technique in which the practitioner shifts their gaze to perceive two overlapping images of themselves, allowing an evasive sidestep that confuses opponents.

rites.name: Seostum
rites.text: A hidden rising strike performed by a warrior who channels a sealed inner power. When the wielder's fury is roused, the strike needs no precise timing, and a dark glow flickers around the fist.

rites.name: Teolus
rites.text: A combat technique in which a fighter swings the back of the hand in a sweeping arc. It is used by a single named warrior in a modern arena brawling tradition.

rites.name: Vornor
rites.text: A hidden technique that two paired fighters can unleash together in a duel. It works like a linked assault, but only certain partner combinations can trigger it, and it leaves the ally poised in a distinct guarding posture.

rites.name: Cerus
rites.text: A leaping strike used by a brawler known as Dorvel in a battle-sport arena. It is performed in close combat from a set range and launches the attacker upward at a defender.

rites.name: Tisteollum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver that a fighter performs to seize an opponent and hurl them to the ground. Two related forms of the same warrior can also execute it.

rites.name: Leoniantium
rites.text: A fighter's low leg maneuver, first taught to one practitioner and later shared with another before being replaced. A variant reuses its motion, and a single opening strike can lead into a follow-up stance.

rites.name: Siallanum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver in which a fighter hoists an opponent onto their shoulders and drops them headfirst, a variant that leaves the user sprawled on the ground afterward. If the hold fails, the user lands face down while still facing the foe.

rites.name: Tilum
rites.text: A close-range grappling maneuver that slams a foe onto the ground and can be held to show the user writhing in pain. A struck standing opponent is always thrown, and a missed connection forces a crouch.

rites.name: Torium
rites.text: A devastating strike technique wielded by a feared brawler in a modern fighting tournament. It can be unleashed as a finishing burst during other powerful combat maneuvers.

rites.name: Nesaulia
rites.text: A coordinated technique used by two fighters in a combat contest after their return to the arena. It is a stance-based maneuver that marks a shared practice between them.

rites.name: Reostilum
rites.text: A deadly maneuver practiced by a warrior named Kazuka, who has used it since first entering a great tournament of combat.

rites.name: Vellosia
rites.text: A fiery energy bolt hurled by a fighter that costs one full gauge segment. Lesser bolts shatter against it, but other enhanced shots can cancel it out.

rites.name: Niasentium
rites.text: A low spinning sweep favored by a pair of martial brawlers across several bouts. Holding a down-back input lets the fighter rise crouched, but they are frozen in place and cannot guard during recovery. Blocking it leaves the attacker briefly reeling.

rites.name: Serenum
rites.text: A heavy strike technique wielded by a fighter in a combat arena. It is one fighter's personal variant of a common basic blow.

rites.name: Tauneolum
rites.text: A two-blow technique that a fighter named Vorsk performs, delivering a rounded, polished strike that echoes twice in quick succession. Known to be practiced by the duelist Serevane since first appearing in the arena.

rites.name: Nontirus
rites.text: A striking technique that a fighter performs by driving the knee forward at an opponent. It is known to appear in the repertoire of a masked combatant from the later years of a tournament line.

rites.name: Carnes
rites.text: A bound-inducing technique wielded by a fighter in a team-based combat contest. Striking with it forces the opponent into a binding state.

rites.name: Nalor
rites.text: A newly devised aerial strike that a fighter with an unusual gift unleashes during a return bout. It launches an opponent-battering assault from the air.

rites.name: Seonia
rites.text: A fighting technique in which the practitioner slides low along the ground and sweeps the opponent's leg with a sharp kick. Two sisters of the same lineage have used it since the earliest contests.

rites.name: Sauliantum
rites.text: A ranged strike drawn from a dark stance, delivered by a warrior who channels a fierce inner force. It forms part of a wrathful fighting posture.

rites.name: Mestus
rites.text: A reversal technique used by a sorcerous surgeon that answers one particular brute. It triggers on its own whenever a hard blow lands during a counter strike.

rites.name: Valaurum
rites.text: A evasive fighting technique in which a combatant dips low to slip an incoming strike, then rapidly alternates strikes from either side. It is practiced by a single wandering fighter across two competitive contests.

rites.name: Vaustium
rites.text: A two-strike maneuver favored by a pair of duelists in an arena of combat. Its second blow shifts the fighter into a new stance, and in team bouts it can be chained onto an ally's timing.

rites.name: Caulliastor
rites.text: A practiced close-range technique used by a skilled fighter, first recorded in a later clash of arts. It is known as a deliberate, repeatable blow.

rites.name: Sentania
rites.text: A swift, stealthy technique used by one fighter in a team brawling contest. It lets the user close distance quickly while staying low and hard to spot.

rites.name: Ameres
rites.text: A combat technique used by a fighter in a brawling tournament for several installments before being dropped from the roster. A modified version survives as a follow-up attack in a kick-based sequence.

rites.name: Corenus
rites.text: A fighter's heavy strike that overwhelms the opponent's guard. It can be thrown through a defender's stance to break through their attack.

rites.name: Veliantor
rites.text: A counter technique a martial warrior uses to turn an incoming blow back on its attacker. The same motion once served as a boastful gesture before the fighting began.

rites.name: Mornium
rites.text: A fighter's strike is a sharpened version of an older jab, used by two bruising warriors in the newest tournament style. It is a refined variant of a basic technique.

rites.name: Raullus
rites.text: A paired striking maneuver in which two fighters swing their tails together. It is performed by a duo working as a team in a tag-style combat contest.

rites.name: Vallenanum
rites.text: A fighter's technique that begins with a low sweeping strike and transitions into a rising hooked kick. It has been adopted by two different practitioners across separate combat tournaments.

rites.name: Naurnium Valiaror
rites.text: A bent-legged sweeping strike that a fighter with a dagger-blade in her stance uses in a tag-team brawl, and that her mechanical partner can also perform.

rites.name: Serilum
rites.text: A bouncing, taunting fighting posture practiced by a skilled duelist from a distant guild. A second warrior from a rival circle can also adopt this posture in team bouts.

rites.name: Mastum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver used by a brawler since his first appearance in an arena contest. In a later tournament it can be linked to a partner's assist, and in another it becomes a combined throw alongside a specific ally.

rites.name: Seostor
rites.text: A fighter's signature strike that a practitioner unleashes against an enormous foe. When the second blow lands, it sets off a twisting spin that throws the opponent off balance.

rites.name: Amaunus
rites.text: A fighting technique practiced by a single combatant since her first appearance in a tournament. In an older handheld contest version, it serves as a basic opener for chaining attacks.

rites.name: Coriantum
rites.text: A bold striking technique used by a fighter and later passed to her daughter. It is performed in combat matches, carried forward across generations of practitioners.

rites.name: Vantum
rites.text: A repeating striking technique practiced by a single fighter, where a second blow follows the first in a natural flow. Adding a forward press after the opening hit shifts the fighter into a quiet, gliding stance, while a different final input unleashes a combined finishing sequence.

rites.name: Cesalia
rites.text: A devastating finishing technique wielded by a sovereign fighter, unleashed in a surge of stored fury. It serves as one of her signature overwhelming strikes.

rites.name: Amornellium
rites.text: A fighter adopts a dual-footed posture that lets them shift between two fighting modes. One practitioner has used this stance in recent years to strike from unexpected angles.

rites.name: Serirus
rites.text: A chained sequence of strikes that must be started by one fighter while their partner stands ready in a darker guise. Its final blow spins the foe into a dazed state, opening the way for another attack.

rites.name: Amiastanum
rites.text: A fighting technique that a single named combatant has used in recent contests. It is a chained sequence of maneuvers leading into an inverted balancing stance.

rites.name: Amisum
rites.text: A coordinated strike technique practiced by a single fighter, where a follow-up blow of the sequence sets off a twisting, spiraling counter-motion. It has been adopted in recent duel traditions.

rites.name: Silium
rites.text: A grappling technique in which a warrior binds a rival's limbs and hurls them away. It is practiced by one fighter of a modern arena tradition.

rites.name: Rillium
rites.text: A combat maneuver that a warrior of the Ruskar lineage performs with a gathering tempest of force. It has been practiced since the most recent great trial of arms.

rites.name: Tiantoria
rites.text: A signature maneuver performed by one fighter, first shown in a recent clash of arenas. It is used in combat as this warrior's trademark technique.

rites.name: Oraurnes Meontus
rites.text: A rapid striking technique used by a warrior order of the forest. It delivers a quick sequence of hits that ends in a forceful finishing blow.

rites.name: Taustor
rites.text: A grappling hurl performed by a brawler that shifts the fighter into a fierce, wild posture afterward. It serves as a gateway into that aggressive battle mode.

rites.name: Telontium
rites.text: A fighting posture used by one warrior since an early tournament era, borrowing the back half of a dodging motion. It shares most of its strikes with a sibling stance and was later hidden from the move list.

rites.name: Telistolor
rites.text: A practiced fighting maneuver that a single warrior has relied on since first entering a major tournament. It is known for its reliability in close combat.

rites.name: Valaseorium
rites.text: A practiced aerial strike used by a skilled physician-fighter inside a team combat contest. It launches an opponent skyward with a sudden upward kick.

rites.name: Varnilles
rites.text: A reckless fist technique that a hulking brawler has used since first appearing in a modern arena contest. It is a wild, unpredictable strike favored by one bruiser.

rites.name: Vorus
rites.text: A grappling technique used by two sisters of a fighting clan that locks an opponent's limb in a throw. It can follow a joint-lock strike, and if the target breaks free, the attacker takes a small wound.

rites.name: Coraustor
rites.text: A practiced striking technique wielded by a certain brawler in a combat tournament. It is a single enhanced blow used during fights.

rites.name: Amaurallum
rites.text: A rising strike delivered by two fighters across several arena bouts, first born as a hidden finishing blow in a combo chain. Partners in a tag match can prepare it ahead of time.

rites.name: Valeostones
rites.text: A two-handed striking technique performed by a fighter named Kelda Morn. It has been practiced since her first public contest in a modern arena.

rites.name: Amintor
rites.text: A fierce striking technique that a fighter performs with a sweeping spinning motion. It is practiced by one warrior and has been used in combat ever since the newest tournament era began.

rites.name: Soranor
rites.text: A deadly lunging strike favored by a duelist of the modern era. It ends a fight in a single blow when properly landed.

rites.name: Mauntornor
rites.text: A fighter's technique that can be held to strike harder and leave a defender less punished. Held longer, it swells into a fiercer blow, and during a burning surge the hold builds faster.

rites.name: Lialaustes
rites.text: A fighter's rapid kicking technique that is used by a single warrior and can also be performed by a towering brute. Its second strike can launch an opponent into the air.

rites.name: Reontum
rites.text: A grappling throw that a fighter has used since first appearing in a contest of martial combat. It lifts an opponent and drives their head down hard.

rites.name: Oreollia
rites.text: A finishing technique a fighter uses on a standing foe. It seizes the opponent from the front and turns a grapple into a throw.

rites.name: Tialleonia
rites.text: A practiced maneuver favored by a single combatant since their first contest in the arena. It is performed as a deceptive, feinting technique to unbalance an opponent.

rites.name: Naulanum
rites.text: A rapid combat maneuver that a fighter learns alongside a particular warrior. It can also be unleashed while slipping low beneath an opponent's guard.

rites.name: Valaseontor
rites.text: A fighter adopts a dark monstrous guise that grants new strikes resembling those of his beast form. Repeating the input returns him to his ordinary shape, and the guise ends when the surge of power runs out.

rites.name: Liantus
rites.text: A flowing, rhythmic strike technique practiced by a single warrior since her first appearance in a grand martial tournament. It is a signature maneuver tied entirely to that one fighter.

rites.name: Marenes
rites.text: A relentless aerial maneuver that a fighter performs in a dueling arena, one that cannot be stopped or deflected once it begins. Practitioners learn it as a signature technique in later training.

rites.name: Amaraulus
rites.text: A signature rising punch passed down by a fighting clan's elder, later taught to a bear-like warrior. Its power grows when the user is in a fierce, focused state.

rites.name: Nantus
rites.text: A grappling craft devised for beasts that were shaped in forced laboratory experiments on wild creatures or grown from cloned ancient reptiles. It turns the raw strength of such engineered bodies into powerful holds and throws.

rites.name: Orirnia
rites.text: A tumbling throw in which a wielder uses a single fighter's acrobatic turn to hurl an opponent over their shoulder. It has been practiced by one skilled warrior in recent years.

rites.name: Valeoria
rites.text: A stealthy low-slung glide that a fighter uses to slip sideways out of an opponent's line. It has been a favored technique of one skilled combatant since the third great tournament cycle.

rites.name: Amastus
rites.text: A blow aimed at the upper body that is quick and hard to get hit by when defending standing or crouching. Its strength is that it cannot be seen coming easily, though some counters can punish it.

rites.name: Tastes
rites.text: A grappling maneuver used by a fierce warrior in a modern combat tournament. It was first seen in an earlier fighting contest as one of that fighter's holds.

rites.name: Valausilus
rites.text: A fighting technique a returning warrior performs in tournament combat. It is a strike used with a sudden lunging motion, learned after the fighter comes back to the arena.

rites.name: Reraustanum
rites.text: A fierce striking technique used by a wandering martial artist who has returned to the fighting circuit. In a later iteration it becomes a special burst that a combatant can unleash for a powerful surge.

rites.name: Sallanum
rites.text: A combat maneuver performed by one fighter in a later era of the arena circuit. It has been removed from the official move list in its newer version, though practitioners can still use it.

rites.name: Cillornanum
rites.text: A close-range striking technique used by a single brawler since its first appearance in a fighting tournament. It drives an armored joint forward into an opponent's body.

rites.name: Velines
rites.text: A bent-leg strike that a fighter named Bob has used since the seventh bout cycle. It was later given a new name, the Spin Heel, in its eighth version.

rites.name: Vostirnus
rites.text: A combat technique in which a fighter rises into the air to strike at a foe. It is performed by a dark warrior in later contests.

rites.name: Amesia
rites.text: A striking technique practiced by a lone fighter in a tag bout. It is a single maneuver used during combat between rival duelists.

rites.name: Cauntes
rites.text: A fighter drives both fists forward in one heavy surge that breaks through an opponent's guard. In a later version it can also shrug off incoming blows while striking.

rites.name: Veonium
rites.text: A forceful striking technique performed by a single combatant in a contest of arena fighters. It is practiced by one skilled fighter and has been part of her repertoire for a number of years.

rites.name: Tallaunia
rites.text: A close-range striking technique performed by a fighter with a heavy, rooted stance. It is used from the second installment of its fighting tradition onward.

rites.name: Sereonanum
rites.text: A rapid combat maneuver employed by a warrior of the Vael clan, first practiced in a later age of duels. It is used as a technique in the fighting arts.

rites.name: Valiarnanum
rites.text: A signature strike wielded by a single warrior ever since their first public appearance in a grand tournament. It is a single attack technique unique to that fighter.

rites.name: Corarnes
rites.text: A tactical maneuver that a fighter performs in combat. Landing its second strike sets off a stunning follow-up effect against the opponent.

rites.name: Corolus
rites.text: A fighter's quick forward kick, long used by a few practitioners, gradually abandoned as newer strikes replace it in later bouts.

rites.name: Oriaranes
rites.text: A combat technique in which a forward leg strike flows into a quick punch, and a later variant adds a sliding dash that can follow it.

rites.name: Orales
rites.text: A pressurized jet of hot vapor hurled forward by a rival fighter in a combat contest. It can be chained after an ally's strike and sometimes sets off a spinning gust.

rites.name: Virnalum
rites.text: A fighting technique used by a brawler during his first appearance in a combat tournament. It is a signature maneuver that marks his entrance into the contest.

rites.name: Riares
rites.text: A grappling strike favored by one fighter, who has used it since first entering the arena. It hooks an opponent with clawed fingers.

rites.name: Teontellium
rites.text: A forward-tumbling evasive technique practiced by a physician-fighter in a tag combat tournament. It is used as a rolling maneuver to slip past an opponent's attacks.

rites.name: Telaunialum
rites.text: A fighter's signature technique, performed by one warrior who has carried it forward since a later clash of the arena.

rites.name: Minum
rites.text: A grappling technique used by a brawler across several bouts, its final strike can be held back for a moment. In later iterations it was dropped, and its command now triggers a different maneuver.

rites.name: Corintostor
rites.text: A spinning strike technique once used by a brawler during an early bout, later abandoned in favor of a heavier shove. It marks a shift in the fighter's combat style.

rites.name: Celia
rites.text: A fighter's rapid two-blow technique that, when the second strike catches a standing foe off guard from the front, flows into a grappling hurl. Pinning the victim against a barrier adds a crushing slam.

rites.name: Orillentus
rites.text: A two-strike technique that a fighter repeats across rounds of contest. When the rhythm is held just right, the second blow stuns the opponent far longer, enabling a looping chain that fighting circles eventually forbade.

rites.name: Valaustium
rites.text: A two-handed strangling technique that a fighter performs in a duel. Once begun, pressing forward during either squeeze shifts the wielder into a feral battle posture.

rites.name: Costanum
rites.text: A fighter's chained kick sequence that a skilled duelist uses in place of an older, plainer low strike. It lets the attacker sweep an opponent's footing with a flourish.

rites.name: Ceorosanum
rites.text: A fighting technique used by a warrior that is a sharpened variant of an older sweeping strike and a branch of a familiar combo chain. Its final blow carries whirling, wind-like force.

rites.name: Cantes
rites.text: A practiced counter move that a wary fighter uses after absorbing two strikes. It snaps back on the foe as a lifting strike, though a quick reader can still slip free by blocking at the exact right instant.

rites.name: Reollasanum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a combatant springs low like a startled hare, then skims forward across the ground in a shimmering slide. It has been passed among several skilled duelists over successive contests.

rites.name: Carnestia
rites.text: A hovering combat stance adopted by winged fighters who drift through the air. While descending, they can automatically guard against strikes aimed at the middle or upper body if they choose not to counterattack.

rites.name: Valires
rites.text: A fighter's readied posture that a warrior adopts for combat. Crackling sparks wreathe the feet on entry, though the glow offers no true force.

rites.name: Relosanum
rites.text: A fighter's striking sequence that begins with a kick and flows into a sidestep stance. Pressing a forward direction during the opening strike returns the fighter to the original footing.

rites.name: Liarnontus
rites.text: A practiced hooking blow that a fighter uses in close combat, first performed in a recent tournament by one particular combatant.

rites.name: Sernus
rites.text: A violent strike is unleashed by a warrior of the Ashen Circle, drawing on a dark inner force. Its power erupts in a sudden, devastating burst during combat.

rites.name: Corilenum
rites.text: A combat technique in which a rapid barrage of blows ends with a low sweeping strike, followed by a spinning kick. The final hit sets off a twisting spiral effect.

rites.name: Cauntia
rites.text: A fighting technique where a combatant hooks a foe's leg with a spinning, whirlwind-like sweep. It is favored by one brawler who has used it since first entering the arena.

rites.name: Amilor
rites.text: A grappling hold that a fighter performs by catching an opponent at the knee and hurling them down. Several combatants have learned it across many generations of contests, and some lose it when a newer maneuver takes its place.

rites.name: Raures
rites.text: A combat maneuver in which a fighter sidesteps a central blow by shifting the body. Wielders of a certain elite lineage have practiced it for many generations.

rites.name: Amerollanum
rites.text: A ritual strike technique used by a single wandering fighter since their earliest contest. It is practiced as a signature maneuver of its user.

rites.name: Teliastium
rites.text: A fighter's technique that follows an initial sweeping blow with a second hit. It serves as an extended version of an earlier, simpler strike.

rites.name: Tiasentes
rites.text: A quiet technique in which a fighter performs a motion that inflicts no harm but fills her reserve of crimson energy. It builds the power used for later bursts of strength.

rites.name: Sintesanum
rites.text: A grappling technique where a fighter seizes an opponent's neck with both hands and squeezes at once. It has been practiced by a skilled brawler for many years.

rites.name: Seorellanum
rites.text: A combat technique performed by a fighter who has returned to the arena after an absence. It is a signature maneuver that combines a leaping strike with a crushing finish.

rites.name: Valaurium
rites.text: A fighter's signature technique that crushes through incoming blows and can rebound an opponent off a barrier. Its power has shifted across releases, sometimes also heating up the user's momentum.

rites.name: Riantium
rites.text: A combat technique in which a fighter strikes twice in quick succession, and in the newer tradition the second blow unleashes a whirling gale.

rites.name: Valinorum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver used by a pair of kinsmen who seize an opponent and fling them across the arena. Facing a barrier, it slams the victim into the surface, and it can also be shared with a partner in team bouts.

rites.name: Lianiria
rites.text: A fighting technique performed by a single practitioner, first shown when she entered the arena. It is a high kicking strike used in combat.

rites.name: Cosium
rites.text: A evasive strike technique in which a fighter drops low and drives an elbow forward. It is adapted by others into a sliding variant, and in some contests it can be queued in advance during a partner's turn.

rites.name: Corianum
rites.text: A fighter's signature kick technique, performed by a spinning drop into a low sweeping strike. It has been used by one combatant since first entering a tournament circuit.

rites.name: Corelia
rites.text: A fighter's technique that resets a combat stance into a volatile, aggressive posture. It belongs to a skilled combatant's personal set of moves.

rites.name: Amauntus
rites.text: A combat technique a rebellious android fighter uses in close-quarters bouts. She can also execute it while facing away from her opponent.

rites.name: Lerneones
rites.text: A heavy overhead strike that drives a foe low to the ground when it lands cleanly. Charging it deepens the blow and can bring a fallen opponent fully airborne.

rites.name: Coraulium
rites.text: A heavy charging strike that a brawler named Morrin unleashes in combat. When it is blocked, it can also smash the opponent into a nearby barrier.

rites.name: Amiantus Taurnentia
rites.text: A mechanical sweeping strike that drops a foe to the ground when it lands. In later duels it can finish a chain of hits by knocking an opponent who tries to recover.

rites.name: Telenes
rites.text: A fighting technique used by a brawler named Gorran Vesh in a combat tournament. It is one of the moves in his personal arsenal.

rites.name: Oraureoles
rites.text: A fighter's combat technique that pairs a sweeping elbow with a rapid snapping kick. It is performed by a single warrior whose style it defines.

rites.name: Meostes
rites.text: A swift strike used by a pair of bear-like fighters, which after its second blow lets the wielder shift into a stalking mode. When a fiery surge is active, that surge is spent to make the second blow ready sooner.

rites.name: Canaullor
rites.text: A fighter's quick sequence of two punches followed by a straight blow, which an opponent can no longer dodge low after blocking the first two strikes.

rites.name: Lestanum
rites.text: A bodily art of releasing pent-up strain at the right moment, practiced by one fighter since her first appearance. When heated, its counter is replaced by a swift, slipping evasion.

rites.name: Amaleontes
rites.text: A signature technique wielded by a single fighter, held by pressing two strike buttons together. Holding the input longer lets the blow be stored and unleashed with greater force.

rites.name: Amerontium
rites.text: A ritual technique wielded by a fighter in a modern arena duel, serving as the combatant's most powerful overwhelming finishing blow.

rites.name: Coriallor Reornastia
rites.text: A devastating technique wielded by a sorceress in a duel, unleashed in bursts of fury. Its command was altered later so it draws only part of a fighter's surge of power without ending that state.

rites.name: Costanium
rites.text: A devastating technique wielded by an aging master, used as a powerful finishing blow. It borrows elements from another fighter's lightning-driven art.

rites.name: Vauneles
rites.text: A tactical technique in which a rapid burst of light and noise is used to stun a foe, giving the user a window to rush in and strike. Warriors of a modern martial tradition employ it as a signature method.

rites.name: Meornium Vastesor
rites.text: A fighter's technique first performed in a later combat tournament, used by one warrior from that point onward. It is a strike that delivers a cold, freezing hit.

rites.name: Seornor
rites.text: A forceful strike that a few named fighters use in every contest they enter. It is known as a signature technique passed among the same practitioners.

rites.name: Ceniastium
rites.text: A deceptive posture where a fighter shifts their weight as if about to strike, drawing an opponent's guard out of position. It is practiced in a tournament combat tradition.

rites.name: Nontum
rites.text: A hurled strike used by a shadowy fighter who first appeared in a combat tournament and later returned with a stronger form. It is a technique tied to that fighter's identity.

rites.name: Amalontes
rites.text: A grappling hold in which one fighter locks an opponent's legs in a twisted coil. It is used by a brawler in a tournament of combatants.

rites.name: Cornor
rites.text: A quick striking technique that a fighter uses in ritual combat. It was first taught to the warriors of a distant coastal clan.

rites.name: Ventium
rites.text: A fighter's crossing blow that a warrior uses in an arena contest. It is one of the techniques a combatant can deploy during a duel.

rites.name: Nolliranum
rites.text: A ritual strike favored by a lineage of fighters, passed from parent to child. It can flow into a charging follow-up once an opening sequence of blows has landed.

rites.name: Caunosor
rites.text: A combat maneuver performed by later mechanical fighters, first passed down from an earlier prototype that reappeared in a tournament. It is a striking technique used in close-quarters bouts.

rites.name: Tiles
rites.text: A fighting technique performed by a single named combatant, first shown when she entered the arena. It is a strike sequence whose execution marks her style in every bout.

rites.name: Ameorium
rites.text: A striking technique in which a fighter drives both knees upward in quick succession. It has been passed down through a family of practitioners.

rites.name: Amesornor
rites.text: A reckless leaping technique that a fighter performs to close distance on an opponent. It was first shown by a brawler in a later bout of a combat tournament.

rites.name: Oranernus
rites.text: A hovering maneuver performed by a physician-fighter in a team combat contest. It lets the user float above the ground while striking an opponent.

rites.name: Cantium
rites.text: A silent strike that cannot be stopped, performed by a line of mechanical fighters. Early models lacked it, but later machines learned to use it as a standard technique.

rites.name: Cantiarnus
rites.text: A single decisive blow reserved for one ruler alone, performed only within a certain fighting arena. It seizes an opponent and hurls them down with crushing force.

rites.name: Telaulium
rites.text: A dangerous fighting technique wielded by a single notable combatant in a modern brawling arena. It is a strike that breaks an opponent's guard.

rites.name: Soranum
rites.text: A strike landed while an opponent is mid-assault gains stronger force and can change into a different outcome. Striking at the exact moment of an enemy's offense sometimes lifts, topples, or stuns them.

rites.name: Manium
rites.text: A fighter's technique in which a single strike is followed quickly by a second blow that extends a basic bodily hit. It is used in combat.

rites.name: Lalum
rites.text: A sweeping technique wielded by a single fighter in a combat arena. It is a move that the warrior uses in battle.

rites.name: Serianium
rites.text: A bruising technique used by a towering brute in a fighting contest. A successful hit leaves the target briefly staggered and unable to act freely.

rites.name: Sontor
rites.text: A close-range striking technique that two fighters used when they first appeared in a combat tournament. It was later passed to a third fighter, then retired and replaced by a different strike.

rites.name: Riastausium
rites.text: A powered-up technique that a fighter can unleash by linking two of their combat moves together. It is available to every combatant in the arena, drawing on a shared style of enhanced strikes.

rites.name: Nelaurus
rites.text: A heavy overhead strike performed by a brawler in later bouts of a tournament. A rival may answer a crushing embrace by delivering the same blow back.

rites.name: Valestia
rites.text: A feinting technique practiced by a martial artist who has used it since a later era of combat trials. It is a deceptive maneuver that baits an opponent into a false opening.

rites.name: Rolauntor
rites.text: A flying technique used by a single fighter since first appearing in a combat tournament. It is a dropping aerial strike performed by hurling the body forward through the air.

rites.name: Telalus
rites.text: A leaping kick to the face that certain fighters have used across several bouts. It is a signature technique shared by a few practitioners who each learned it in their own time.

rites.name: Tillosanum
rites.text: A fighting technique that one warrior has used in combat since first appearing in a major tournament of bouts. It is a maneuver tied to a single practitioner.

rites.name: Reostirnes
rites.text: A fighter spins twice in a row, sweeping the legs of an opponent. Two members of a combat troupe are known to perform this technique.

rites.name: Serosaullia
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a practitioner swings one leg in a sweeping arc to strike an opponent. It is passed between a few skilled fighters who have trained in it for many years.

rites.name: Seores
rites.text: A staggering feint used by a martial artist since the sixth tournament cycle. The fighter wavers as though intoxicated, then snaps a sudden jab through the opening.

rites.name: Amantus
rites.text: A brutal technique in which a warrior brings both clenched fists down together onto an opponent. It is favored by a hulking brawler who has relied on it for years.

rites.name: Terolor
rites.text: A fighter's signature combat technique passed between kin, a leaping double strike that still sometimes sends an opponent spinning through the air after it lands.

rites.name: Meraulum
rites.text: A combat maneuver practiced by a fighter of a later era. Its second strike sets off a spiraling twist that disrupts the opponent's guard.

rites.name: Telanentia
rites.text: A hidden combined maneuver that two linked fighters can perform only while they stand side by side as partners. It is known only to the pair who share its secret.

rites.name: Teleolor
rites.text: A brutal two-handed blow where the wielder strikes twice in quick succession with a heavy fist. It is practiced by a mechanical champion and its later successors.

rites.name: Maulus
rites.text: A fighter's signature combat maneuver that debuted in a later tournament clash. It forms the middle strikes of a combined assault, sitting between an opening slash and a closing spinning finisher.

rites.name: Meosanum
rites.text: A fiery technique wielded by a warrior of a distant clan, unleashed as a devastating strike. It was first mastered in the third cycle of the great tournament.

rites.name: Coraunes
rites.text: A calculated strike technique used by a scientist in a modern fighting tournament. It applies crushing force to an opponent's body in close combat.

rites.name: Corantesium
rites.text: A raw blow that no guard can stop, usable only by two bear-like warriors in later contests. It can empty an entire vitality gauge in a single strike, and it was later stripped from the fighting rules.

rites.name: Valantelum
rites.text: A fighter's technique that lifts an opponent through a sudden surge of metallic motion, carried by a combatant who first appeared in a recent contest of arms. It is a signature maneuver passed down through one warrior's training.

rites.name: Rosteoranum
rites.text: A two-handed strike technique practiced by fighters, passed between combatants in a long-running contest of skill. Two lone warriors rely on it as their signature sudden attack.

rites.name: Cauntium
rites.text: A signature technique that a single fighter has used since a particular tournament. It is a move in the fighter's repertoire, passed down through repeated practice.

rites.name: Celeornum
