rites.name: Nintia
rites.text: A evasive maneuver a fighter performs by stepping away from an opponent. In an earlier form of the craft, retreating while in a transformed state would instead send the user into a flip.

rites.name: Oriarnus
rites.text: A fighter's strike that charges the battle fervor of its user. After it lands, the user can instantly drop low, but only while that fervor is burning or has been spent.

rites.name: Varisus
rites.text: A three-strike rhythm of rapid leg blows used by a wandering duelist from the newest rulebook. The third strike can be redirected into a different poise, and the final blow spins the fighter upward before a quick recovery.

rites.name: Teleoloses Valialum
rites.text: A sweeping low kick that drops into a sharp finishing strike. Two fighters have trained it since a later tournament era, and one other combatant learned it in a tag contest.

rites.name: Cirnium Telenus
rites.text: A whip-like technique performed by a fighter in a tournament of combat. It is one of the strikes used in the brawling arena.

rites.name: Viranum
rites.text: A whirling strike technique performed by a fighter in a combat arena, which serves as one of the ways to activate a heightened battle state.

rites.name: Tauranum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver that a pair of duelists can use to hurl an opponent sideways. In later arenas, the impact can crack the ground beneath the fighters.

rites.name: Ceollium Cirium
rites.text: A spinning throwing-star strike is a fighting technique that a warrior has used since first appearing in a major tournament of martial combatants.

rites.name: Rillor Oranelanum
rites.text: A fighting maneuver favored by a martial artist who rises into a soaring strike. In later contests, it can cause an opponent to rebound into the air.

rites.name: Vauseostium
rites.text: A defensive technique in which a fighter deflects an incoming blow and, when successful, can follow with a chained counterattack. The chosen follow-up depends on whether the deflected strike was a fist or a foot.

rites.name: Cania
rites.text: A practiced close-quarters maneuver used by a fighter named Kenmar in a contest of arena combat. It is performed as a striking technique within a tournament of hand-to-hand duels.

rites.name: Tasintes
rites.text: A fighter's strike that replaces an older kick in the combat repertoire. It serves as a special aggressive opener and can also be performed by a fallen twin form during certain encounters.

rites.name: Meorum Cernum
rites.text: A grappling technique in which a mechanical fighter hurls a foe against a barrier, crushing them for additional harm when the wall is close behind.

rites.name: Tiarum
rites.text: A swift technique used by a combatant who has trained with it since her first appearance in a rebellion. Its input was later adjusted, and the older command was given to a separate related technique.

rites.name: Mestor Orintanum
rites.text: A fighter's rolling strike technique, performed by one warrior since first entering the arena. It is a move that spins the body low and sweeps toward an opponent.

rites.name: Santium
rites.text: A two-part strike favored by a wandering duelist across several eras of contests. When performed during a surge of inner fire, its follow-up lifts the opponent off their feet.

rites.name: Raunium
rites.text: A toxic haze that a warrior of the mask-clad kind can unleash in combat. It is a technique that has been known since its first appearance in a famous duel.

rites.name: Ceornialium
rites.text: A grappling maneuver that a fighter performs in close quarters, and which can shatter the ground beneath the combatants. In a later iteration, it can cause an even more violent eruption.

rites.name: Maulus Reosus
rites.text: A glowing technique wielded by a single fighter, first displayed in a recent arena clash. It is a precise slicing strike that lights up the air as it lands.

rites.name: Veostor
rites.text: A fighter's rapid sequence of punches, performed as a chained technique. It has been practiced by one warrior since her first appearance in the arena.

rites.name: Oriles
rites.text: A combat maneuver practiced by two fighters in a tournament of arena contests. It is a technique passed between partners who bring it into their bouts.

rites.name: Telisteolor
rites.text: A fighter's rising knee attack that, when it lands on an upright foe, flows into a seizing grip for added harm. A later version drops the grip and instead barrels through incoming strikes.

rites.name: Seraunes
rites.text: A forceful striking technique favored by one fighter in tag bouts. Its second impact sends the target into a helpless tumble.

rites.name: Telalus Saror
rites.text: A flying striker lifts into the sky, then sweeps across and fires a beam back the opposite way, unblockable and dealing full strike damage. Any mechanical foe struck by the beam goes wild and spins into a flailing punch.

rites.name: Siror Nintia
rites.text: A tag-team strike technique performed by two fighters working together in a modern arena contest. It lets a pair of combatants launch a coordinated attack as a single shared maneuver.

rites.name: Rallistanum
rites.text: A swift leg technique used by a dark-clad fighter since their first appearance. A master of the same style later learns it as well.

rites.name: Laures
rites.text: A refined fighting posture that a warrior adopts in the current era. It is an improved form of an older guard, sharpened into a more powerful version.

rites.name: Vilenium
rites.text: A striking technique used by one fighter, a close-quarters strike that chills the opponent. It has been part of a fighting style for many years.

rites.name: Coranisus
rites.text: A practiced fighting technique that a single skilled combatant has used in later duels since a certain tournament. It is known as a signature maneuver tied to one particular warrior.

rites.name: Telauntum Seraullus
rites.text: A hidden combat technique that only one fighter can perform, and only when a specific ally stands beside them. It is a coordinated maneuver that depends on the partnership between the two.

rites.name: Montelor
rites.text: A grappling technique where the user passes some of their own vitality into a foe. If the bond is severed, the user drains a portion of the foe's vitality instead.

rites.name: Telostium
rites.text: A brutal technique that a dark-cloaked fighter uses to strike a foe's inner body. A winged counterpart of the same warrior can also perform it.

rites.name: Meornianum
rites.text: A tumbling backward leap that strikes a foe with the feet as they land. The user's legs remain dangerous from behind, and the leap can be chained into a follow-up blow.

rites.name: Tentum Nantes
rites.text: A evasive tumbling maneuver passed down through a fighting bloodline, used by a warrior and later by his father. In team bouts it can be queued up in advance by a partner.

rites.name: Taurnor
rites.text: A fighting technique once performed by a single practitioner across several generations of combat. It was later dropped from the repertoire of the discipline.

rites.name: Amollesor
rites.text: A fighter turns their body around and strikes backward with one leg. The technique has been used by a single practitioner since first appearing in an early tournament-style contest.

rites.name: Neollanum
rites.text: A fighter's quick hooking strike that a skilled combatant has used for years, with its motion sped up in later training. A successful connection lets the wielder slide smoothly into a follow-up hammering attack.

rites.name: Neolauntus
rites.text: A reverse-thrust technique performed by a fighter who first appeared in a recent brawling clash of arena champions. It is a maneuver the fighter uses to launch an attack from an unusual stance.

rites.name: Cauneontes
rites.text: A fighting technique practiced by two warriors in a modern arena. Its second strike shifts the flow into a darker stance called Velkara.

rites.name: Moria
rites.text: A low, rapid strike thrown by a brawler who swaps out an older kick-and-punch sequence. If the opening it targets is caught by surprise, the blow is guaranteed to land.

rites.name: Cilium
rites.text: A throwing technique that one warrior alone performs, taking the place of an older leaping slam maneuver the same fighter once relied upon. It is passed down through later training regimens.

rites.name: Naurnum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver used by one fighter since an early team-battle contest, and in that contest it can be queued up during a partner's turn.

rites.name: Teliarnanum
rites.text: A piercing strike used by a sky-dancer that has been adapted over several releases. In its later form it can only be unleashed while gliding through the air.

rites.name: Vontianum
rites.text: A grappling strike favored by a brawler of long standing. Early versions could lift a foe when it caught them off guard, but that ability was dropped in a later revision.

rites.name: Coranum
rites.text: A practiced strike favored by one fighter in later tournament matches. Its second blow can set off a twisting counter effect in newer contests.

rites.name: Corallus
rites.text: A two-part sweeping strike used by a warrior across several arena contests. The second blow can bind the foe in place or ignite a burning surge of combat energy.

rites.name: Meollus
rites.text: A kick technique that a fighter uses against an opponent who is in the air. Striking a leaped foe with it sets off a spinning whirlwind.

rites.name: Coriastes
rites.text: A combat technique where a fighter endures blows from middle and high strikes while continuing their own attack. Low strikes can break the hold, and a grab during it cannot be escaped.

rites.name: Nalum
rites.text: A fighter's technique of spinning the body backward into a tight rolling ball. It is used by one combatant as a signature maneuver from their first appearance onward.

rites.name: Amorneollor
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a combatant hurls an opponent with a fiery rising motion. A modified version of the technique can be entered while in a crouching stance, a refinement added later to the art.

rites.name: Naullanum
rites.text: A combat technique passed among a line of mechanical fighters, first performed by one of them and later inherited by others. A prototype model can also perform it when it returns to a later contest.

rites.name: Corestirum
rites.text: A fighter's striking technique that leads the user into a flowing dance-like stance afterward. Practitioners across generations have passed it on as a signature form.

rites.name: Nontes
rites.text: A quick striking technique used by a physician-trained fighter in a combat tournament. It is delivered in rapid succession to overwhelm an opponent.

rites.name: Corenus Caustum
rites.text: A grappling maneuver used by two fighters in a hall of duels. One fighter takes the opponent's momentum and hurls them to the floor.

rites.name: Ralintor
rites.text: A thrown strike favored by a masked wrestler who has used it since first appearing in a fighting tournament. It is performed as a whirling grapple that sends the opponent flying.

rites.name: Ceontes
rites.text: A rapid combat maneuver in which a fighter hooks the leg and follows with a heel strike. It is favored by a masked wrestler in later contests.

rites.name: Corontus
rites.text: A fighting technique used by one brawler from a later round of combat contests. It is a rapid striking attack that launches the opponent into the air.

rites.name: Serirnia Telialirnia
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a wielder strikes four times with clawed limbs in rapid succession. It is practiced by two bear-like warriors who use it in combat.

rites.name: Valastonia
rites.text: A swift forward surge a fighter enters by sprinting and holding the forward command while distant from a foe. Later revisions let the surge begin even when standing close before an opponent.

rites.name: Amesarum
rites.text: A swift striking technique performed by one fighter that, when landing on an opponent who is airborne, sets off a spinning gale.

rites.name: Serollentor
rites.text: A grappling strike delivered from one side that a fighter can break out of, but only through a specific counter. Later iterations made the escape a single press.

rites.name: Orarialanum
rites.text: A fighting maneuver performed by three combatants in every bout they enter. In certain later contests, its opening strike sends the opponent into a bound.

rites.name: Cerauntium
rites.text: A fighting maneuver favored by a single brawler, first displayed when that fighter entered the arena roster. It is a technique performed in close combat.

rites.name: Oraniallor
rites.text: A grappling strike where a fighter binds an opponent's body and then releases the coiled force in a sudden, violent surge. It is a technique favored by a single brawler in a tournament-era fighting circuit.

rites.name: Tastanum
rites.text: A spinning strike delivered by a masked grappler, first used in a later chapter of a combat tournament. In subsequent chapters it can also be launched while the fighter faces away from the foe.

rites.name: Reonum
rites.text: A fighter's technique that a warrior of the modern arena performs to deliver a hard attack. It belongs to one combatant's personal repertoire of blows.

rites.name: Causia
rites.text: A quick charging strike used by later mechanical fighters, first adopted by an earlier automaton model after its return to the arena.

rites.name: Taurnes Masteontus
rites.text: A deliberate attack made by a single fighter who hurls a reputation-damaging assault at an opponent. The move has been used since its first appearance in a recent contest of skill.

rites.name: Viallus
rites.text: A grappling maneuver used by every brawler of the Jaqon Carver lineage since the fifth tournament. It replaces an older lifting hold and is known by a different name in one eastern region.

rites.name: Valarinum
rites.text: A fighter's sudden low strike that a combatant has used since an early tournament era, taking the place of a spinning kick technique. It is favored by one warrior in the arena.

rites.name: Mallontium
rites.text: A rhythmic striking technique performed by a single fighter in close combat. It has been practiced by one combatant since a later era of the arena circuits.

rites.name: Neralles
rites.text: A fighting stance adopted by one combatant in a team battle contest. It lets the fighter tumble low across the ground to evade incoming strikes.

rites.name: Ciasollia
rites.text: A fighter's rapid two-strike sequence, performed with the right limb, that once ended with a shift into a new guard. Later sequences replaced it with a different technique.

rites.name: Valolum Solianor
rites.text: A fighting technique that a warrior performs to shift their body into a new guard position. Its final strike can be queued early in certain training systems, and when a surge of fury is active, the entire chain lands with reliable force.

rites.name: Marnus
rites.text: A fighting technique used by a warrior since her first appearance in a grand clash of bloodlines. It is a sweeping strike that spins the body into an attack.

rites.name: Oraustenus
rites.text: A fighter's combat technique launched from a right punch into a raised kick. Its second strike shifts the user into a new guarding posture, and a later combination is built upon it.

rites.name: Cintollia
rites.text: A ruinous technique wielded by a warrior that drains a foe's spirit once a prior strike lands. Its use is restricted to a rare, monstrous form of the same fighter.

rites.name: Vauror
rites.text: A practiced evasive maneuver that a single fighter performs to slip back into a sheltered stance. It stayed hidden from the training scrolls for years before it was finally recorded.

rites.name: Sarnus Restontia
rites.text: A fighting technique that a practitioner performs in a sharp coiling strike. Once executed, it leaves the user in a sidelong, slithering stance.

rites.name: Rilonia
rites.text: A grappling hurl performed by a masked wrestler that can be intensified by tapping the guiding motions swiftly. While a surge of fervor is active, spectators roar as the stronger version lands.

rites.name: Taunia
rites.text: A tactical maneuver employed by a mechanized guardian line, advancing sideways and then unleashing an explosive strike. It has been practiced by these defenders since an early training era, beginning with a heavy-armed warrior.

rites.name: Valineornia
rites.text: A fighter's technique that delivers a sharp blow to a staggered opponent. A heavier version exists, and in later contests the blow can set off a spinning counter.

rites.name: Tonteonor
rites.text: A low, sliding fighting stance taken by a skilled dueling performer. It opens the way to chains of strikes that can be linked together in quick succession.

rites.name: Seornus
rites.text: A fighter's signature maneuver linking a particular sequence of strikes into a lunging finishing attack. It is performed by one warrior in a recent, modern-era tournament.

rites.name: Sereornium
rites.text: A combat maneuver practiced by a fighter in a team bout of tournament champions. It is a technique belonging to one warrior's personal repertoire.

rites.name: Serontia
rites.text: A rising strike used by a brawler who first appeared in a fighting contest and later by a smaller variant. Its follow-up blow can be held back, and in one version it can be queued during a partner swap.

rites.name: Sernum Veosornia
rites.text: A swift forward strike thrown by a fighter from a brief moment of stillness. It can only be learned during a particular trial of a certain battle sequence.

rites.name: Teleolanum
rites.text: A coiled strike technique in which a practitioner releases two crackling arcs of energy at once. It is taught as a signature technique of a returning master of the old arts.

rites.name: Vaunarnia
rites.text: A soft, sliding technique used by a single fighter, performed while settling into a crouched stance. It belongs to a particular combat style.

rites.name: Reontistor
rites.text: A fighter's open-handed strike, thrown while swaying, that sends a foe skidding flat on their back when it lands cleanly. Its power grows over time and it can ignite the fighter's surge.

rites.name: Oraunanum Riallium
rites.text: A reversal technique used by one fighter in a modern tag brawl, in which an opponent's own momentum is turned back against them. It has been performed by the same warrior since a second tournament.

rites.name: Sisorium
rites.text: A striking technique once called by another name, performed by a fighter who has used it since first entering a combat tournament. It is a repeatable maneuver tied to one particular combatant.

rites.name: Amornanum
rites.text: A signature strike favored by three fighters across every bout they enter. Its second blow shifts into a darker form of the same motion.

rites.name: Coroleosor
rites.text: A spinning strike in which a fighter drives a heel around in a wide arc to hit a rival. It was later replaced by a flipping variant and is absent from some training manuals.

rites.name: Amisia
rites.text: A rapid rising blow performed by a brawler who favors a particular fighting style. It can be queued early during a partner exchange, letting a companion's turn set up its timing.

rites.name: Nenaustes
rites.text: A fighter's crouched-forward posture with one hand held at the hip and the other arm dangling ready to strike. From it, the fighter can guard and parry but cannot step, leap, or dodge.

rites.name: Orinialia
rites.text: A tumbling throw technique performed by a hulking brawler during close-quarters clashes. It sends an opponent flailing through the air after a grapple.

rites.name: Orestiles
rites.text: A grappling throw that a fighter performs to seize a rival and force them down. It has been used by one brawler since first being seen in a tournament.

rites.name: Cellium
rites.text: A swift, leaping striker technique first developed by a martial artist from the wandering performers. Its later strikes can be held back and delayed by the practitioner.

rites.name: Oranostum
rites.text: A fighter's combat maneuver that can drive an opponent into a barrier after an opening blow lands. The follow-up strike only comes out if that opening blow connects.

rites.name: Ceolastanum
rites.text: A fighter's signature heavy blow that unleashes a stored surge of energy against an opponent. It serves as the wielder's empowered finishing technique.

rites.name: Orerium Nauleosium
rites.text: A bruising spinning technique a fighter can unleash in a team bout. It can be set up by an ominous ritual move and is used to strike a rival who blocks it without staggering them.

rites.name: Rosteolles
rites.text: A practiced maneuver favored by one fighter since her first appearance in a recent tournament. It is a signature technique she relies on in combat.

rites.name: Amollanum
rites.text: A fighting technique passed between students of a single academy, starting with one practitioner and later taken up by a classmate. Its opening strike can cause the opponent to rebound helplessly.

rites.name: Orisestor
rites.text: A fighting technique performed by a duelist and her demonic alter form. It is one of the combat maneuvers used in a modern martial tournament.

rites.name: Amiarnosum
rites.text: A bright acrobatic maneuver performed by a fighter in a duel, a rearward flip that carries a whirling, spinning quality through the air.

rites.name: Oriarnollum
rites.text: A fighter's signature technique that unleashes a surging assault upon a foe struck while standing or airborne. If the strike is blocked instead, the user slips into an empowered, heightened state.

rites.name: Rilium
rites.text: A fighting technique practiced by a single martial artist, which in later contests leaves an opponent briefly stunned after it lands.

rites.name: Telontia
rites.text: A fighter's technique in which a warrior charges low and strikes with a rolling, sweeping blow. It is used by a single named combatant since first appearing in a famed arena tournament.

rites.name: Nintasor
rites.text: A swift stepping maneuver that three fighters carry into every contest they enter. It strikes low and sweeps an opponent's leg from beneath them.

rites.name: Valeontes
rites.text: A dark strike technique borrowed from an earlier brutal maneuver, used by a masked warrior in later contests. Its use can also summon a whirling gale.

rites.name: Telostor
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a warrior lashes an opponent with a sudden, silvery sweep. It has been passed among practitioners since a tag-team trial of arenas.

rites.name: Teleonor
rites.text: A fighting maneuver that a particular combatant has relied on since first entering the arena. It is a swinging strike used in close combat.

rites.name: Telintor
rites.text: A swift technique that a warrior can only unleash while in a particular charged stance. Using it ignites a heated surge that drives the fighter's combat intensity upward.

rites.name: Leolirnanum
rites.text: A dancing maneuver that a fighter performs in a flashy sequence of strikes. A second blow can flow directly into a gliding follow-up when the right direction is held.

rites.name: Telones
rites.text: A clumsy strike delivered with the trailing leg by a physician-fighter in a tag-team arena bout. It is a weak technique that rarely decides a match.

rites.name: Corialor Orestus
rites.text: A fighting technique that a single combatant performs with a sweeping aerial spin. It has been used by one practitioner since she first entered the arena.

rites.name: Oristes
rites.text: A tumbling strike favored by a single ruler since a shared tournament. Since a later contest it also pursues targets in mid-air.

rites.name: Rausenia
rites.text: A short-range lunging technique performed by a hulking brawler in a team combat arena. It is used to grapple and throw an opponent to the ground.

rites.name: Sarum Leolium
rites.text: A dazzling stylized maneuver performed by a single fighter in a combat arena. It was first displayed in a recent tournament and is favored by that one warrior.

rites.name: Orareostum
rites.text: A swift combined strike performed by a fighter who joins a team bout. It is a rapid chain of blows delivered in succession.

rites.name: Lerinium
rites.text: A fighting technique practiced by two rival duelists, ending in a strike that flows into a hazardous counter-form. In certain tournaments, the closing blow can be queued early by a partner.

rites.name: Vianeornium
rites.text: A move that cannot be blocked, used by an elder warrior in a fighting contest on a home console. It is a technique passed down among combatants.

rites.name: Tiarium
rites.text: A fighter crouches with both arms lifted overhead, opening a set of follow-up strikes. Paired with another stance, it lets the user slip backward quickly without the usual sidestep.

rites.name: Neontoria
rites.text: A sudden combat technique in which a fighter wields dark energy to cut past an opponent's guard. It has been used by a single warrior since first appearing in a major tournament.

rites.name: Valintium
rites.text: A fighter's striking technique that homes in on its target and, once landed, sets off a spiraling twist. It is performed by a single practitioner.

rites.name: Oreornalium
rites.text: A defensive counter technique passed from a fighter to her offspring across generations. Its rear-facing variant turns the guard away from the opponent, and it can be reached through a specific button sequence from a related stance.

rites.name: Tilles
rites.text: A fighter's technique that unleashes a forceful burst of energy. A stronger variant can be triggered during a special charged state, and the technique was later replaced in a newer generation by a different maneuver.

rites.name: Telarnanum Telauntia
rites.text: A fighter's forward strike that shifts the wielder into a new guard position. Landing it cleanly leaves a foe briefly staggered, though a practiced opponent can recover by moving forward.

rites.name: Tarium Veollia
rites.text: A slow, low technique favored by a brawler since first appearing in a tournament of arena combat. It strikes from the ground in a sudden, curling motion.

rites.name: Ralles
rites.text: A combat maneuver used by a fighter who has a hidden inner power. It replaces an older technique and can be performed without first knocking an opponent to the ground. The fighter cannot use it during moments when that power is sealed away.

rites.name: Riastanum
rites.text: A bursting fire technique wielded by a warrior who has mastered it. It is unleashed as a sudden, scorching attack in close combat.

rites.name: Corallor
rites.text: A fighter's technique first used in a earlier competitive bout, though it was only officially recorded in a later tag-team contest. It is performed by one particular combatant.

rites.name: Lirnes
rites.text: A combat maneuver that a fighter performs in a tournament arena, replacing an older technique. Its second strike releases a spinning gale and wears down an opponent's health even when blocked.

rites.name: Mosus Valiastanum
rites.text: A fighter's technique that begins a strike and then turns into a grab when it lands cleanly against an upright foe from the front. It has been part of a warrior's repertoire for several generations.

rites.name: Tarnauranum
rites.text: A soaring technique in which a fighter spins through the air and strikes with a kick. It was revived in a later contest after its practitioner returned to the arena.

rites.name: Ristanum
rites.text: A heavy strike technique favored by a line of mechanical fighters, later refined so that holding the button builds a stronger, longer-reaching blow. A related variant also exists among some hulking warriors.

rites.name: Valintor Ceoloses
rites.text: A closing strike within a fighter's combat sequence that opens the way to a radiant burst of power and triggers a heat surge when it lands.

rites.name: Amorium
rites.text: A ferocious technique wielded by a brawler in a combat arena, unleashed as a powerful finishing surge when his inner fury peaks.

rites.name: Cesor
rites.text: A fighting technique performed by a single combatant who has used it since first entering the arena. Two other fighters' signature sequences are built upon its pattern.

rites.name: Vernaullia
rites.text: A looping strike of the arm used by a masked wrestler in a modern arena. It has been a signature technique since the fighter's first appearance in a tournament.

rites.name: Amaulantus
rites.text: A combat technique used by a fighter across several contests, which in later bouts can trigger a binding effect that holds the opponent in place.

rites.name: Telaunium
rites.text: A fighting technique favored by one practitioner of a skilled martial circle since the second great tournament of paired duelists. It is a chain of kicks that leaves out an expected blow.

rites.name: Seraullanum Amasanum
rites.text: A fighting technique performed by a masked duelist across two combat contests. It is a signature strike that the user unleashes during matches against rival challengers.

rites.name: Lirauntium
rites.text: A borrowed technique that a fighter performs in ring combat. It is passed through several tournament bouts of brawling.

rites.name: Coraulanum
rites.text: A fighting technique where a lowering blow flows into a rising kick to the head. It has been passed between two related practitioners in the wider lineage.

rites.name: Valiasor
rites.text: A low sweeping strike used by a fighter and their hidden alternate persona. It can flow into a second stance when the combatant enters a specific input sequence.

rites.name: Mialium
rites.text: A two-blow striking technique passed among several brawlers across many contests. Its second blow can be held back for a moment, and it can also open a stronger combined assault.

rites.name: Amaulor
rites.text: A fast spinning kick technique passed between two fighters over several tournaments. One fighter's version launches a foe while the other's does not, and a later rival move eventually replaces it.

rites.name: Valernes Amollanum
rites.text: A shifting technique used by a dark-winged fighter since first appearing in the arena. It lets the user sink and slip beneath an opponent's guard.

rites.name: Contisum
rites.text: A mental maneuver used by a scholar-fighter in a combat contest, bending an opponent's thoughts to disrupt their footing. It is practiced in arenas where rival duelists test their skill.

rites.name: Caurnus Oreostes
rites.text: A fighting maneuver that a combatant performs to shift into a balanced one-legged stance. In later iterations it also sends the opponent rebounding off a barrier.

rites.name: Masintium
rites.text: A fighter rushes forward and drives a low swinging strike upward, then follows with a sweeping backhand blow. It is a two-part combo chained from a single raised punch.

rites.name: Liarania
rites.text: A practiced thrust technique used by a skilled duelist. A follow-up input after the first strike shifts the attacker into a second, flowing maneuver.

rites.name: Tarnurne
rites.text: Tarnurne is a cinder-throated wyrm-spirit that coils within the marrow of the Brurnadeld Ki-realm's oldest mountains, a hungry inheritance that once slept beneath the sediment of E6's first age. It was drawn forth as a separate sovereign of hunger, rising to strip the arcs of entire ridgelines before its appetite was bound back into the greater body that bears its ember.

rites.name: Morestock
rites.text: Morestock is a dormant ember-form that wakes inside the lungs of certain Ki-born wardens when their oath frays, granting a brief wingless sky-glide and bursts of cinder-light. Its wardens call it the second breath, and the Brurnadeld cloisters keep its ledger sealed.

rites.name: Halorurdeld
rites.text: Halorurdeld is a radiant state of purified will in which a bearer sheds an inherited shadow and burns it away from the inside. In the Brurnadeld cosmos it is treated as a rite of clean release rather than conquest, and only those who have faced their own darkness can enter it.

rites.name: Moruldene
rites.text: Moruldene is a concept of the Brurnadeld Realm of Ki, a shelving-principle that exists only while the Three Futures remain unresolved and the ending still branches. It is said to hold every outcome ever considered, filed in a Library that has no walls.

rites.name: Serorneonus
rites.text: Serorneonus is a concept of Brurnadeld, a idea that surfaces when the ending branches and the Library shelves each outcome. It is tied to the Ki realm and to the early groves and growing kingdoms of the first sovereign's age.
